context: “[Then] Elisha prayed, … Lord, … open his eyes, that he may see. And the Lord [did open] the eyes of the young man; and he [did see that] the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: The scriptures teach that we are to “[stand] steadfastly in the faith of that which is to come.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: “Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.”
footnote_text: Matthew 6:9–10; see also Doctrine and Covenants 65:6.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: In that day He will not come “wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger,”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: but He will appear “in the clouds of heaven, clothed with power and great glory; with all the holy angels.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: We will hear “the voice of the archangel, and … the trump of God.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: The sun and the moon will be transformed, and “stars [will] be hurled from their places.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: You and I, or those who follow us, “the saints … from [every quarter] of the earth,”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: “shall be quickened and … caught up to meet him,”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: and those who have died in righteousness, they too will “be caught up to meet him in the midst … of heaven.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: Then, a seemingly impossible experience: “All flesh,” the Lord says, “shall see me together.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: How will it happen? We do not know. But I testify it will happen—exactly as prophesied. We will kneel in reverence, “and the Lord shall utter his voice, and all the ends of the earth shall hear it.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: “It shall be … as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: “[Then] the Lord, … the Savior, shall stand in the midst of his people.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: There will be unforgettable reunions with the angels of heaven and the Saints upon the earth.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: But most important, as Isaiah declares, “All the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God,”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: and He “shall reign over all flesh.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: In that day the skeptics will be silent, “for every ear shall hear … , and every knee shall bow, and every tongue shall confess”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: Thy Kingdom Come
context: Today is Easter. We rejoice with Christians all over the world in His glorious Resurrection and in our own promised resurrection. May we prepare for His coming by rehearsing these glorious events over and over in our own minds and with those we love, and may His prayer be our prayer: “Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.”

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: I told him, “Because I am not a member of the Church.”
footnote_text: Please note that “although the sacrament is for Church members, the bishopric should not announce that it will be passed to members only, and nothing should be done to prevent nonmembers from partaking of it” (Handbook 2: Administering the Church [2010], 20.4.1).

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: What responsibility do we have as members of the Church of Jesus Christ? President Joseph Fielding Smith expressed it as follows: “We have these two great responsibilities. … First, to seek our own salvation; and, second, our duty to our fellow men.”
footnote_text: Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Joseph Fielding Smith (2013), 294.

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: These, then, are the main responsibilities that our Father has assigned to us: seeking our own salvation and that of others, with the understanding that in this statement, salvation means reaching the highest degree of glory that our Father has provided for His obedient children.

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: For someone who has come to understand that, because of the Atonement of Jesus Christ, exaltation is truly within reach, failing to obtain it constitutes damnation. Thus, the opposite of salvation is damnation, just like the opposite of success is failure. President Thomas S. Monson has taught us that “men cannot really long rest content with mediocrity once they see excellence is within their reach.”
footnote_text: Thomas S. Monson, “To the Rescue,” Ensign, May 2001, 49; Liahona, July 2001, 58.

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: If we are to do God’s will, if we are to be responsible to Him, we must begin by learning, understanding, accepting, and living according to His will for us. The Lord has said, “Wherefore, now let every man learn his duty, and to act in the office in which he is appointed, in all diligence.”

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: “Then it doesn’t matter which way you go,” says the cat.
footnote_text: Lewis Carroll, Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland (1920), 89.

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: However, we know that the path that leads to the “tree, whose fruit [is] desirable to make one happy”

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: 7—“the way, which leadeth unto life”—is narrow. It takes effort to journey along the path, and “few there be that find it.”

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: Nephi teaches us that “the words of Christ will tell you all things what ye should do.”

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: Then he adds that “the Holy Ghost … will show unto you all things what ye should do.”

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: Whether we have learned about the Restoration of the gospel, a particular commandment, the duties associated with serving in a calling, or the covenants we make in the temple, the choice is ours whether or not we act according to that new knowledge. Each person chooses freely for himself or herself to enter into a sacred covenant such as baptism or the temple ordinances. Because swearing oaths was a normal part of people’s religious lives in antiquity, the old law stated that “ye shall not swear by my name falsely.”

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: However, in the meridian of time, the Savior taught a higher way of keeping our commitments when He said that yes meant yes and no meant no.

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: A powerful example of the firm determination to meet His commitment with His Father comes from the Savior’s experience of having a man sick with palsy brought to Him to be healed. “When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.”

speaker: Jorge F. Zeballos
title: If You Will Be Responsible
context: I am impressed by and admire the attitude of the leper who came to the Lord, “beseeching him, and kneeling down to him, and saying unto him, If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: In the day that God the Father called upon His Only Begotten Son to make man in Their image and likeness, He blessed His children, saying, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it, and have dominion … over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: “Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples.”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: We become fruitful as we abide in Christ and as we “take upon [ourselves His] name [and] … serve him to the end”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: The starting point of a response that yields much fruit is to “be meek and lowly in heart.”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: We can then more fully come unto Christ as we yield to the enticings of the Holy Spirit and keep all the covenants we have made.

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: Laboring in the spirit of charity is not a duty but a joy. Challenges become opportunities to build faith. We become “witnesses of [the goodness of] God at all times and in all things, and in all places that [we] may be in, even until death.”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: All of us can and should become fully engaged in the work of salvation. The Savior has given us the following responsibility with a promise: “I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: Our physical bodies are a blessing from God. We received them for the purposes of fulfilling Heavenly Father’s work “to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: The body enables Heavenly Father’s obedient spirit children to experience life on earth.

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: Because of His love for us, Heavenly Father has provided that all His faithful children who do not or are not able to enjoy the blessings of a covenant marriage and children or a fulness of those blessings for reasons not of their making will, in the Lord’s appointed time, enjoy these blessings.
footnote_text: See Handbook 2: Administering the Church (2010), 1.3.3; Ezra Taft Benson, “To the Single Adult Sisters of the Church,” Ensign, Nov. 1988, 96–97.

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: To subdue the earth and have dominion over every living thing is to control these things so they fulfill the will of God

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: as they serve the purposes of His children. Subduing includes gaining mastery over our own bodies.

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: It does not include being helpless victims of these things or using them contrary to the will of God.

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: Developing the ability to subdue the things of the earth begins with humility to recognize our human weakness and the power available to us through Christ and His Atonement. For “Christ hath said: If ye will have faith in me ye shall have power to do whatsoever thing is expedient in me.”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: The challenges facing human society today, including immorality, pornography, armed conflict, pollution, substance abuse, and poverty, flourish because many in the world have turned themselves over by choice “to the will of the devil and the flesh”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: rather than to the will of God. “They seek not the Lord to establish his righteousness, but every man walketh in his own way, and after the image of his own god, whose image is in the likeness of the world.”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: “… If thou wilt turn unto me, and hearken unto my voice, and believe, and repent of all thy transgressions, and be baptized, even in water, in the name of mine Only Begotten Son, … ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost, asking all things in his name, and whatsoever ye shall ask, it shall be given you.”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: Faithful Latter-day Saints who understand their divine potential and rely wholeheartedly on the power available through the Atonement of the Lord Jesus Christ are strengthened in their natural weakness and “can do all things.”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: “God is faithful, [and] will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.”

speaker: Joseph W. Sitati
title: Be Fruitful, Multiply, and Subdue the Earth
context: “For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: I am intrigued by the words of Isaiah, who called the Sabbath “a delight.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: What did the Savior mean when He said that “the sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath”?

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: In Hebrew, the word Sabbath means “rest.” The purpose of the Sabbath dates back to the Creation of the world, when after six days of labor the Lord rested from the work of creation.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: When He later revealed the Ten Commandments to Moses, God commanded that we “remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: Later, the Sabbath was observed as a reminder of the deliverance of Israel from their bondage in Egypt.
footnote_text: See Deuteronomy 5:14–15. People who choose to work seven days a week are essentially in bondage—to work or perhaps to money, but they are slaves nevertheless. A millionaire who works seven days a week is a rich slave.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: Perhaps most important, the Sabbath was given as a perpetual covenant, a constant reminder that the Lord may sanctify His people.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: In addition, we now partake of the sacrament on the Sabbath day in remembrance of the Atonement of Jesus Christ.
footnote_text: See Doctrine and Covenants 59:12. Prior to His Crucifixion, the Lord introduced the sacrament among His disciples at the Feast of the Passover (see Matthew 26:26–28; Mark 14:22–24). The resurrected Lord instituted the sacrament in remembrance of His Atonement among the people of ancient America (see 3 Nephi 18:1–12; Moroni 4:1–3; 5:2) and restored it in modern times (see Doctrine and Covenants 20:77, 79). Partaking of the sacrament renews our covenant made at baptism to keep His commandments (see Doctrine and Covenants 20:68).

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: Again, we covenant that we are willing to take upon us His holy name.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: The Savior identified Himself as Lord of the Sabbath.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: It is His day! Repeatedly, He has asked us to keep the Sabbath
footnote_text: See Exodus 31:13; Leviticus 19:3, 30; 26:2; Doctrine and Covenants 68:29.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: or to hallow the Sabbath day.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: How do we hallow the Sabbath day? In my much younger years, I studied the work of others who had compiled lists of things to do and things not to do on the Sabbath. It wasn’t until later that I learned from the scriptures that my conduct and my attitude on the Sabbath constituted a sign between me and my Heavenly Father.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: “And inasmuch as ye do these things with thanksgiving, with cheerful hearts and countenances, … the fulness of the earth is yours.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: Imagine the scope of that statement! The fulness of the earth is promised to those who keep the Sabbath day holy.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: The Sabbath provides a wonderful opportunity to strengthen family ties. After all, God wants each of us, as His children, to return to Him as endowed Saints, sealed in the temple as families, to our ancestors, and to our posterity.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: We make the Sabbath a delight when we teach the gospel to our children. Our responsibility as parents is abundantly clear. The Lord said, “Inasmuch as parents have children in Zion … that teach them not to understand the doctrine of repentance, faith in Christ the Son of the living God, and of baptism and the gift of the Holy Ghost by the laying on of the hands, when eight years old, the sin be upon the heads of the parents.”
footnote_text: Doctrine and Covenants 68:25; emphasis added; see also Moses 6:58–62.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: “We counsel parents and children to give highest priority to family prayer, family home evening, gospel study and instruction, and wholesome family activities. However worthy and appropriate other demands or activities may be, they must not be permitted to displace the divinely-appointed duties that only parents and families can adequately perform.”
footnote_text: First Presidency letter, Feb. 11, 1999; quoted in Handbook 2: Administering the Church (2010), 1.4.1.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: “Teach ye diligently … , that you may be instructed more perfectly … in doctrine, in the law of the gospel, in all things that pertain unto the kingdom of God.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: I have seen this firsthand. Several years ago, my dear wife Wendy determined to learn how to do family history research. Her progress at first was slow, but little by little she learned how easy it is to do this sacred work. And I have never seen her happier. You too need not travel to other countries or even to a family history center. At home, with the aid of a computer or mobile device, you can identify souls who are yearning for their ordinances. Make the Sabbath a delight by finding your ancestors and liberating them from spirit prison!

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: Make the Sabbath a delight by rendering service to others, especially those who are not feeling well or those who are lonely or in need.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: “Then shalt thou delight thyself in the Lord.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: Think of this: In paying tithing, we return one-tenth of our increase to the Lord. In keeping the Sabbath holy, we reserve one day in seven as His. So it is our privilege to consecrate both money and time to Him who lends us life each day.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: Now, as this conference comes to a close, we know that wherever we live we are to be examples of the believers among our families, neighbors, and friends.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: The Sabbath Is a Delight
context: I conclude with the farewell plea of Moroni, as he closed the Book of Mormon. He wrote, “Come unto Christ, and be perfected in him, and deny yourselves of all ungodliness; and if ye shall deny yourselves of all ungodliness, and love God with all your might, mind and strength, then … are ye sanctified in Christ.”

speaker: Rosemary M. Wixom
title: Discovering the Divinity Within
context: Job said, “The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.”

speaker: Rosemary M. Wixom
title: Discovering the Divinity Within
context: We come into this world “trailing clouds of glory.”
footnote_text: “Ode: Intimations of Immortality from Recollections of Early Childhood,” The Complete Poetical Works of William Wordsworth (1924), 359.

speaker: Rosemary M. Wixom
title: Discovering the Divinity Within
context: “The Family: A Proclamation to the World” teaches that each one of us “is a beloved spirit son or daughter of heavenly parents” and “each has a divine nature and destiny.”
footnote_text: “The Family: A Proclamation to the World,” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2010, 129.

speaker: Rosemary M. Wixom
title: Discovering the Divinity Within
context: Elaine Cannon, a former Young Women general president, said, “There are two important days in a woman’s life: The day she is born and the day she finds out why.”
footnote_text: Elaine Cannon, in “‘Let Me Soar,’ Women Counseled,” Church News, Oct. 17, 1981, 3.

speaker: Rosemary M. Wixom
title: Discovering the Divinity Within
context: We identify with our divine nature as we feel and give the love of our Father in Heaven. We have the agency to nurture it, let it flourish, and help it grow. Peter said we are given “precious promises” that we “might be partakers of the divine nature.”

speaker: Rosemary M. Wixom
title: Discovering the Divinity Within
context: If you ever question that spark of divinity within you, kneel in prayer and ask Heavenly Father, “Am I really Thy daughter, and dost Thou love me?” Elder M. Russell Ballard said, “One of the sweetest messages the Spirit will relay is how the Lord feels about you.”
footnote_text: M. Russell Ballard, “Women of Righteousness,” Ensign, Apr. 2002, 72; Liahona, Dec. 2002, 42.

speaker: Rosemary M. Wixom
title: Discovering the Divinity Within
context: We are His. Paul said, “The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God.”

speaker: Rosemary M. Wixom
title: Discovering the Divinity Within
context: Often the first Primary song we learn is “I Am a Child of God.”
footnote_text: See “I Am a Child of God,” Hymns, no. 301.

speaker: Rosemary M. Wixom
title: Discovering the Divinity Within
context: President Dieter F. Uchtdorf said, “God sent you here to prepare for a future greater than anything you can imagine.”
footnote_text: Dieter F. Uchtdorf, “Living the Gospel Joyful,” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2014, 121.

speaker: Rosemary M. Wixom
title: Discovering the Divinity Within
context: Later that night her sister sent her a text and quoted Elder Jeffrey R. Holland when he said: “Don’t give up. … Don’t you quit. You keep walking. You keep trying. There is help and happiness ahead. … It will be all right in the end. Trust God and believe in good things to come.”
footnote_text: Jeffrey R. Holland, “An High Priest of Good Things to Come,” Ensign, Nov. 1999, 38; Liahona, Jan. 2000, 45.

speaker: Rosemary M. Wixom
title: Discovering the Divinity Within
context: Recently, Sharon Eubank, the director of Humanitarian Services and LDS Charities, told of an experience shared by Elder Glenn L. Pace. There was widespread drought and extreme famine in Ethiopia in the mid-1980s. To provide relief, feeding stations with water and food were created for those who could get to them. An old man who was starving was walking a long distance to get to a feeding station. He was passing a village when he heard the cry of a baby. He searched until he found the baby sitting on the ground next to his dead mother. Picking up the baby, the man continued to walk 25 miles (40 km) to the feeding station. When he arrived, his first words were not “I’m hungry” or “Help me.” They were “What can be done for this baby?”
footnote_text: See Glenn L. Pace, “Infinite Needs and Finite Resources,” Ensign, June 1993, 52; Tambuli, Mar. 1995, 18–19.

speaker: Rosemary M. Wixom
title: Discovering the Divinity Within
context: I promise that as you seek to discover the depth of the divine nature that lies within you, you will begin to further magnify your precious gift. Let it guide you to become His daughter, walking the path back to Him—where we will be “restored to that God who gave [us] breath.”

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: Worthy of Our Promised Blessings
context: “… Our happiness in mortal life, our joy and exaltation are dependent upon how we respond to these persistent, compelling physical desires.”
footnote_text: Boyd K. Packer, “The Plan of Happiness,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2015, 26–27.

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: Worthy of Our Promised Blessings
context: My dear sisters, both young and not so young, I have felt a great anxiety as I have prepared this talk. As Alma the Younger expressed, “I wish from the inmost part of my heart … that ye would … call on his holy name, and watch and pray continually, that ye may not be tempted above that which ye can bear, … that ye may be lifted up at the last day.”

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: Worthy of Our Promised Blessings
context: Later, Mormon also testified that in Alma’s day, Korihor, the anti-Christ, “did preach … , leading away the hearts of … many women.”

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: Worthy of Our Promised Blessings
context: Many in today’s world are looking for instant gratification and instant knowledge on the Internet. In contrast, we will be exceedingly blessed if we exercise faith and patience and go to our Heavenly Father, the source of all truth, with our concerns. So many answers and assurances can come through daily searching and studying the scriptures and with sincere and pleading prayer, but there are no such promises on the Internet. The prophet Jacob testifies: “For the Spirit speaketh the truth and lieth not. Wherefore, it speaketh of things as they really are, and of things as they really will be.”

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: Worthy of Our Promised Blessings
context: “… The Atonement, which can reclaim each one of us, bears no scars. That means that no matter what we have done or where we have been or how something happened, if we truly repent, He has promised that He would atone. And when He atoned, that settled that. There are so many of us who are thrashing around … with feelings of guilt, not knowing quite how to escape. You escape by accepting the Atonement of Christ, and all that was heartache can turn to beauty and love and eternity.”
footnote_text: Boyd K. Packer, Ensign or Liahona, May 2015, 28.

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: Worthy of Our Promised Blessings
context: Besides repentance, what helps or tools have we been given to help us stay clean and virtuous? Our Primary children and young women all know and sing the song “Scripture Power.”

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: Worthy of Our Promised Blessings
context: There are also great blessings and protecting promises associated with the proper wearing of our temple garment. I have come to feel that I am symbolically putting on royal robes given me by my Heavenly Father. I testify, sisters, that when we strive to wear the garment properly, our Father recognizes it as a great sign of our love and devotion to Him. It is a sign of the covenants we have made with Him, and He has promised, “I, the Lord, am bound when ye do what I say; but when ye do not what I say, ye have no promise.”

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: Worthy of Our Promised Blessings
context: Understandably, many have expressed that our Father’s promised blessings are just “way too far away,” particularly when our lives are overflowing with challenges. But Amulek taught that “this life is the time … to prepare to meet God.”

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: Worthy of Our Promised Blessings
context: It is not the time to receive all of our blessings. President Packer explained: “‘And they all lived happily ever after’ is never written into the second act. That line belongs in the third act, when the mysteries are solved and everything is put right.”
footnote_text: Boyd K. Packer, “The Play and the Plan” (Church Educational System fireside for young adults, May 7, 1995), 2, si.lds.org.

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: Worthy of Our Promised Blessings
context: However, a vision of our Father’s incredible promised blessings must be the central focus before our eyes every day—as well as an awareness “of the multitude of his tender mercies”

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: Worthy of Our Promised Blessings
context: I testify that our bodies are sacred gifts from our Heavenly Father and that as we keep our lives pure and clean through the atoning sacrifice of our Savior and keep the vision of our Father’s promised rewards daily in front of us, we will one day receive “all that [our] Father hath.”

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: I am grateful that we may gather together with faithful women such as Lisa—the sister in the video—who are pure in heart, who love the Lord and serve Him, even amid their own trials. Lisa’s story reminds me that we must love one another and see in one another the beauty of the soul. The Savior taught, “Remember the worth of souls is great in the sight of God.”

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: Whether we are age 8 or 108, each of us is “precious in [His] sight.”

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: Over the summer I visited with a lovely young mother of daughters. She shared with me her feeling that our young women need a cause, something to help them feel valued. She knew that we may discover our individual and eternal worth by acting in accordance with our divine purpose in mortality. Tonight, this beautiful and remarkable choir sang words that teach our purpose. Through test and trial, even through fear and in the midst of despair, we have valiant hearts. We are resolved to do our part. We are here to serve a righteous cause.
footnote_text: See “As Zion’s Youth in Latter Days,” Hymns, no. 256.

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause

title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause

His cause is the good news, “the glad tidings, … that he came into the world, even Jesus, to be crucified for the world, and to bear the sins of the world, and to sanctify the world, and to cleanse it from all unrighteousness; that through him all might be saved.”

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause

footnote_text: “How Great the Wisdom and the Love,” Hymns, no. 195.

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: I testify that as we follow His example, love God, and serve one another with kindness and compassion, we may stand in purity, “blameless before God at the last day.”

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: We choose to serve the Lord in His righteous cause that we may become one with the Father and with the Son.
footnote_text: See John 17:20–23; 4 Nephi 1:15–17; Doctrine and Covenants 35:2; 38:27; Moses 6:68.

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: The prophet Mormon boldly declared, “For we have a labor to perform whilst in this tabernacle of clay, that we may conquer the enemy of all righteousness, and rest our souls in the kingdom of God.”

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: The early Church leaders and pioneers of the past pressed forward with heroic courage and determined faithfulness to establish the restored gospel and build temples where ordinances of exaltation could be performed. The pioneers of the present, meaning you and me, also press forward in faith, “to labor in [the Lord’s] vineyard for the salvation of the souls of men.”

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: And, as President Gordon B. Hinckley taught, “How magnificent will be the future as the Almighty rolls on His glorious work … through the selfless [service] of those whose hearts are filled with love for the Redeemer of the world.”
footnote_text: Gordon B. Hinckley, “Stay the Course—Keep the Faith,” Ensign, Nov. 1995, 72.

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: Before we were born, we accepted our Heavenly Father’s plan “by which [we] could obtain a physical body and gain earthly experience to progress toward perfection and ultimately realize [our] divine destiny as heirs of eternal life.”
footnote_text: “The Family: A Proclamation to the World,” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2010, 129.

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: Of this premortal covenant, Elder John A. Widtsoe explained: “We agreed, right then and there, to be not only saviors for ourselves but … saviors for the whole human family. We went into a partnership with the Lord. The working out of the plan became then not merely the Father’s work, and the Savior’s work, but also our work. The least of us, the humblest, is in partnership with the Almighty in achieving the purpose of the eternal plan of salvation.”
footnote_text: John A. Widtsoe, “The Worth of Souls,” Utah Genealogical and Historical Magazine, Oct. 1934, 189.

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: Here in mortality we have again covenanted to serve the Savior in the work of salvation. By participating in sacred priesthood ordinances, we pledge that we will embark in the service of God with heart, might, mind, and strength.

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: But perhaps most humbling to me was to hear a single adult sister declare with the fire of pure testimony that the most important work we can do is to prepare for marriage and family. Although this is not her experience, she knows that family is the very heart of the work of salvation. “The divine plan of happiness enables family relationships to be perpetuated beyond the grave.”
footnote_text: “The Family: A Proclamation to the World,” 129.

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: In the work of salvation, there is no room for comparison, criticism, or condemnation. It is not about age, experience, or public acclaim. This sacred work is about developing a broken heart, a contrite spirit, and a willingness to use our divine gifts and unique talents to do the Lord’s work in His way. It is having the humility to fall on our knees and say, “O my Father, … not as I will, but as thou wilt.”

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: In the strength of the Lord, we “can do all things.”

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: We continually seek His guidance in prayer, in the scriptures, and in the whisperings of the Holy Ghost. One sister, faced with an overwhelming assignment, wrote, “Sometimes I wonder if the sisters in the early history of the Church didn’t, like us, put their heads on their pillows at night and pray, ‘Whatever tomorrow brings, will Thou help me through it?’” Then she wrote, “One of the blessings is [that] we have each other and we are in this together!”

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: Recently, you may have read about Sister Ella Hoskins, who at 100 years old was called to help the young women in her ward with Personal Progress.
footnote_text: See Marianne Holman Prescott, “She Just Doesn’t Quit,” Church News, Sept. 6, 2015, 15.

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: From a gentle lady, so full of the Spirit of the Lord that she glowed with pure light, I was reminded that to shine with the beauty of holiness, to stand with the Savior, and to bless others, we must be clean. Purity is possible through the grace of Christ as we deny ungodliness and choose to love God with might, mind, and strength.

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: The Apostle Paul taught, “Flee … youthful lusts: … follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.”

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: None of us is perfect. We have all made mistakes. But we repent so that we may be better and “retain the name [of Christ] written always in [our] hearts.”

speaker: Carol F. McConkie
title: Here to Serve a Righteous Cause
context: May we choose to serve a righteous cause as valiant emissaries of our Lord Jesus Christ. Let us stand together and “with a song in [our] heart[s] move forward, living the gospel, loving the Lord, and building [His] kingdom.”

But remember, our weaknesses can help us to be humble and turn us to Christ, who will “make weak things become strong.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: God Is at the Helm
context: In last October’s general conference, I invited listeners to follow Brigham Young’s counsel to stay on the Old Ship Zion, which is The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, and to hold on with both hands.
footnote_text: See M. Russell Ballard, “Stay in the Boat and Hold On!” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2014, 89–92.

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: God Is at the Helm
context: Since then, I am happy to know that some of my family and others were listening and have asked me this question: “What’s in the Old Ship Zion that we should hang on to?” I reminded them of what President Brigham Young said: “We are on the old ship Zion. … [God] is at the helm and will stay there. … He dictates, guides and directs. If the people will have implicit confidence in their God, never forsake their covenants nor their God, He will guide us right.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: God Is at the Helm
context: And make no mistake about it: the Lord directs His Church through living prophets and apostles. This is the way He has always done His work. Indeed, the Savior taught, “Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard

speaker: M. Russell Ballard

Further, we warn that the disintegration of the family will bring upon individuals, communities, and nations the calamities foretold by ancient and modern prophets.”
footnote_text: “The Family: A Proclamation to the World,” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2010, 129.

speaker: M. Russell Ballard

title: God Is at the Helm

speaker: Richard J. Maynes
title: The Joy of Living a Christ-Centered Life
context: The ancient prophet Isaiah stated, “But now, O Lord, thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand.”

speaker: Richard J. Maynes
title: The Joy of Living a Christ-Centered Life
context: Brothers and sisters, I was born into a multigenerational Latter-day Saint family, so the blessings and joy of having the gospel of Jesus Christ as the basis of our family culture was woven into our everyday life. It wasn’t until my full-time mission as a young man that I realized the incredibly positive impact the fulness of the gospel of Jesus Christ has on those who have never previously experienced its blessings in their lives. This verse in Matthew reflects the process that people who are converted to the gospel of Jesus Christ experience: “The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field, which a man found and covered up; then in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.”

speaker: Richard J. Maynes
title: The Joy of Living a Christ-Centered Life
context: This is what the king said to Ammon after finding himself in this life-and-death situation: “If thou wilt spare me I will grant unto thee whatsoever thou wilt ask, even to half of the kingdom.”

speaker: Richard J. Maynes
title: The Joy of Living a Christ-Centered Life
context: After the prophet Lehi and his family left Jerusalem in 600 b.c., they wandered approximately eight years in the wilderness until they finally arrived in a land they called Bountiful, which was near the seashore. Nephi describes their life of tribulation in the wilderness this way: “We had suffered many afflictions and much difficulty, … even so much that we cannot write them all.”

speaker: Richard J. Maynes
title: The Joy of Living a Christ-Centered Life
context: While living in Bountiful, Nephi was charged by the Lord with the responsibility to build the ship which would take them across the sea to the promised land. After they arrived in the promised land, great conflicts continued to arise between the people who centered their lives in Christ and the nonbelievers, who followed the examples of Laman and Lemuel. Ultimately, the risk of violence between the two groups was so great that Nephi and those who followed the teachings of the Lord separated themselves and fled into the wilderness for safety. At this point in time, some 30 years after Lehi and his family left Jerusalem, Nephi makes a well-documented and somewhat surprising statement, especially after recording in the scriptures the many afflictions and tribulations they had faced for so long. These are his words: “And it came to pass that we [did live] after the manner of happiness.”

context: Our family motto doesn’t say, “It will all work out now.” It speaks of our hope in the eternal outcome—not necessarily of present results. Scripture says, “Search diligently, pray always, and be believing, and all things shall work together for your good.”

speaker: Neill F. Marriott
title: Yielding Our Hearts to God
context: This doesn’t mean all things are good, but for the meek and faithful, things—both positive and negative—work together for good, and the timing is the Lord’s. We wait on Him, sometimes like Job in his suffering, knowing that God “maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.”

speaker: Neill F. Marriott
title: Yielding Our Hearts to God
context: True worship begins when our hearts are right before the Father and the Son. What is our heart condition today? Paradoxically, in order to have a healed and faithful heart, we must first allow it to break before the Lord. “Ye shall offer for a sacrifice unto me a broken heart and a contrite spirit,”

speaker: Neill F. Marriott
title: Yielding Our Hearts to God
context: I have struggled to banish the mortal desire to have things my way, eventually realizing that my way is oh so lacking, limited, and inferior to the way of Jesus Christ. “His way is the path that leads to happiness in this life and eternal life in the world to come.”
footnote_text: “The Living Christ: The Testimony of the Apostles,” Ensign or Liahona, Apr. 2000, 3; emphasis added.

speaker: Neill F. Marriott
title: Yielding Our Hearts to God
context: Some may think they have failed too many times and feel too weak to change sinful acts or worldly desires of the heart. However, as covenant Israel, we don’t just try and try on our own to change. If we earnestly appeal to God, He takes us as we are—and makes us more than we ever imagined. Noted theologian Robert L. Millet writes of “a healthy longing to improve,” balanced with the spiritual “assurance that in and through Jesus Christ we are going to make it.”
footnote_text: Robert L. Millet, After All We Can Do: Grace Works (2003), 133.

title: What Lack I Yet?
context: President Harold B. Lee taught, “Every one of us, if we would reach perfection, must [at] one time ask ourselves this question, ‘What lack I yet?’”
footnote_text: Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Harold B. Lee (2000), 197.

speaker: Larry R. Lawrence
title: What Lack I Yet?
context: The Holy Ghost doesn’t tell us to improve everything at once. If He did, we would become discouraged and give up. The Spirit works with us at our own speed, one step at a time, or as the Lord has taught, “line upon line, precept upon precept, … and blessed are those who hearken unto my precepts, … for unto him that receiveth I will give more.”

speaker: Larry R. Lawrence
title: What Lack I Yet?
context: A perfect time to ask, “What lack I yet?” is when we take the sacrament. The Apostle Paul taught that this is a time for each of us to examine ourselves.

speaker: Larry R. Lawrence
title: What Lack I Yet?
context: The atoning sacrifice of the Savior is what makes perfection or sanctification possible. We could never do it on our own, but God’s grace is sufficient to help us. As Elder David A. Bednar once observed: “Most of us clearly understand that the Atonement is for sinners. I am not so sure, however, that we know and understand that the Atonement is also for saints—for good men and women who are obedient, worthy, and conscientious and who are striving to become better.”
footnote_text: David A. Bednar, “The Atonement and the Journey of Mortality,” Ensign, Apr. 2012, 42; Liahona, Apr. 2012, 14.

speaker: Larry R. Lawrence
title: What Lack I Yet?
context: Be persistent, brothers and sisters, but never be discouraged. We will have to go beyond the grave before we actually reach perfection, but here in mortality we can lay the foundation. “It is our duty to be better today than we were yesterday, and better tomorrow than we are today.”
footnote_text: Joseph Fielding Smith, Doctrines of Salvation, comp. Bruce R. McConkie, 3 vols. (1954–56), 2:18.

speaker: Larry R. Lawrence
title: What Lack I Yet?
context: Years ago I read these words of President Spencer W. Kimball, which had a lasting impact on me. He said: “I have learned that where there is a prayerful heart, a hungering after righteousness, a forsaking of sins, and obedience to the commandments of God, the Lord pours out more and more light until there is finally power to pierce the heavenly veil. … A person of such righteousness has the priceless promise that one day he shall see the Lord’s face and know that he is.”
footnote_text: Spencer W. Kimball, “Give the Lord Your Loyalty,” Ensign, Mar. 1980, 4; Tambuli, Feb. 1981, 47.

speaker: Quentin L. Cook
title: Shipshape and Bristol Fashion: Be Temple Worthy—in Good Times and Bad Times
context: The prophet Lehi declared, “If there be no righteousness there be no happiness.”
footnote_text: 2 Nephi 2:13. This scripture is part of a parallelism in the Book of Mormon. It is interesting that many of the prophets whose writings and sermons are included in the Book of Mormon used this literary approach to emphasize important doctrinal concepts. See, for example, 2 Nephi 9:25 (Jacob) and 2 Nephi 11:7 (Nephi).

speaker: Quentin L. Cook
title: Shipshape and Bristol Fashion: Be Temple Worthy—in Good Times and Bad Times
context: The adversary has been successful in planting a great myth in the minds of many people. He and his emissaries declare that the real choice we have is between happiness and pleasure now in this life and happiness in a life to come (which the adversary asserts may not exist). This myth is a false choice, but it is very seductive.

speaker: Quentin L. Cook
title: Shipshape and Bristol Fashion: Be Temple Worthy—in Good Times and Bad Times
context: The ultimate noble purpose of God’s plan of happiness is for righteous disciples and covenant families to be united in love, harmony, and peace in this life

title: Shipshape and Bristol Fashion: Be Temple Worthy—in Good Times and Bad Times
context: and attain celestial glory in the eternities with God the Father, our Creator; and His Beloved Son, Jesus Christ, our Savior.

speaker: Quentin L. Cook
title: Shipshape and Bristol Fashion: Be Temple Worthy—in Good Times and Bad Times
context: Initially I didn’t understand the point he was making. I soon learned the history and meaning of the nautical phrase “shipshape and Bristol fashion.” At one time Bristol was the second busiest port in the United Kingdom. It had a very high tidal range of 43 feet (13 m), the second highest in the world. At low tide when the water receded, the old ships would hit bottom and fall on their sides, and if the ships were not well built, they would be damaged. In addition, everything that was not carefully stowed away or tied down would be thrown in a chaotic fashion and ruined or spoiled.
footnote_text: See Wiktionary, “shipshape and Bristol fashion,” wiktionary.org.

speaker: Quentin L. Cook
title: Shipshape and Bristol Fashion: Be Temple Worthy—in Good Times and Bad Times
context: While the fluctuation of the tide in the Bristol Channel is somewhat predictable and can be prepared for, the storms and temptations of this life are often unpredictable. But this we know: they will come! In order to overcome the challenges and temptations that each of us inevitably faces, it will require righteous preparation and the use of divinely provided protections. We must determine to be temple worthy regardless of what befalls us. If we are prepared, we shall not fear.

speaker: Quentin L. Cook
title: Shipshape and Bristol Fashion: Be Temple Worthy—in Good Times and Bad Times
context: Happiness in this life and happiness in the life to come are interconnected by righteousness. Even in the period between death and the Resurrection, “the spirits of those who are righteous are received into a state of happiness, which is called paradise, a state of rest, a state of peace.”

speaker: Quentin L. Cook
title: Shipshape and Bristol Fashion: Be Temple Worthy—in Good Times and Bad Times
context: At the commencement of the Savior’s earthly ministry in Israel and later among the Nephites, the Savior addressed the issue of happiness both in this life and in eternity. He stressed ordinances, but He also placed great emphasis on moral behavior. For example, disciples would be blessed if they would hunger and thirst after righteousness, be merciful, be pure in heart, be peacemakers, and follow other basic moral principles.
