Faith, hope, and charity—the pure love of Christ—will abound in our homes and lives, bringing in their wake peace, joy, and happiness.”
footnote_text: Marion G. Romney, “The Book of Mormon,” Ensign, May 1980, 67.

speaker: LeGrand R. Curtis Jr.
title: There Is Power in the Book
context: The greatest power of the Book of Mormon is its impact in bringing us closer to Jesus Christ. It is a strong witness of Him and His redeeming mission.
footnote_text: See, for example, the title page of the Book of Mormon; 1 Nephi 11; 2 Nephi 25; Mosiah 16; 18; Alma 5; 12; Helaman 5; 3 Nephi 9; Mormon 7.

speaker: LeGrand R. Curtis Jr.
title: There Is Power in the Book
context: Through it we come to understand the majesty and power of His Atonement.
footnote_text: See, for example, 2 Nephi 2; 9; Mosiah 3; Alma 7; 34.

speaker: LeGrand R. Curtis Jr.
title: There Is Power in the Book
context: It teaches His doctrine clearly.

speaker: LeGrand R. Curtis Jr.
title: There Is Power in the Book
context: And because of the magnificent chapters describing the visit of the risen Christ to the Nephites, we see and experience Him loving, blessing, and teaching those people and come to understand that He will do the same for us if we come to Him by living His gospel.

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: Among the most unforgettable characters in scripture is Alma the Younger. Though he was the son of a great prophet, he lost his way for a time and became a “wicked and an idolatrous man.” For reasons we can only guess, he actively opposed his father and sought to destroy the Church. And because of his eloquence and persuasiveness, he experienced great success.

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: But Alma’s life changed when an angel of the Lord appeared to him and spoke with a voice of thunder. For three days and three nights, Alma “was racked with eternal torment, … even with the pains of a damned soul.” And then, somehow, a faint memory brought light to the darkness of his mind—an eternal truth, taught by his father: that Jesus Christ would come “to atone for the sins of the world.” Alma had long ago rejected such concepts, but now his “mind caught hold upon this thought,” and he humbly, earnestly placed his trust in Christ’s atoning power.

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: But when Alma saw that his people were forgetting God and lifting themselves up in pride and contention, he chose to resign from public office and dedicate himself “wholly to the high priesthood of the holy order of God,”

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: Heartbroken, Alma turned his back on the city Ammonihah.

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: Just think about it: he was told to return to the people who hated him and were hostile toward the Church. It was a dangerous and perhaps life-threatening assignment. But Alma did not hesitate. “He returned speedily.”

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: Alma had been fasting many days when he entered the city. There he asked a complete stranger if he would “give to an humble servant of God something to eat.”

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: Amulek was a well-to-do, well-known citizen of Ammonihah. Although he came from a long line of believers, his own faith had grown cold. He later confessed, “I was called many times and I would not hear; therefore I knew concerning these things, yet I would not [believe]; therefore I went on rebelling against God.”

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: But God was preparing Amulek, and when Amulek met Alma, he welcomed the Lord’s servant into his home, where Alma stayed for many days.

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: His message was not “Stand back. I’ll handle this.” Rather it was “Come, follow me.”

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: He inspired, invited, instructed, and then trusted His followers “to do the things which ye have seen me do.”
footnote_text: Joseph Smith Translation, Matthew 26:25 (in the Bible appendix).

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: Share with them the words of the angel to Amulek—that the blessing of the Lord shall rest upon them and their house.

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: Perhaps you have, over the years, become less committed in your discipleship. Perhaps the fire of your testimony has dimmed. Perhaps you have distanced yourself from the body of Christ. Perhaps you have become disillusioned or even angry. Like some of the ancient Church of Ephesus, you may have left your “first love”

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: He took to heart the scripture “If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.”

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: Learn from Alma and Amulek
context: I urge you to heed His call, for surely you will receive the harvest of heaven. The blessings of the Lord will rest upon you and your house.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: That He May Become Strong Also
context: “[Now] I have been some fifty-four years a member of the Twelve Apostles. I have traveled with that and other quorums now for sixty years; and I want to say to this assembly that I was just as much sustained by the power of God while holding the office of a Teacher, and especially while officiating in the vineyard as a Priest, as I ever was as an Apostle. There is no difference in this so long as we do our duty.”
footnote_text: Wilford Woodruff, “The Rights of the Priesthood,” Deseret Weekly, Mar. 17, 1894, 381.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: That He May Become Strong Also
context: That wonderful spiritual possibility of no difference is suggested in the Lord’s description of the Aaronic Priesthood as an “appendage” of the Melchizedek Priesthood.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: That He May Become Strong Also
context: The word appendage means the two are connected. This connection is important to the priesthood becoming the force and the blessing it can be, in this world and forever, for it “is without beginning of days or end of years.”

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: That He May Become Strong Also
context: “To have the privilege of receiving the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, to have the heavens opened unto them, to commune with the general assembly and church of the Firstborn, and to enjoy the communion and presence of God the Father, and Jesus the mediator of the new covenant.”

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: That He May Become Strong Also
context: That is why we must teach by example and by testimony that the words of the great Melchizedek Priesthood leader King Benjamin are true.
footnote_text: Alma 13:6–9 suggests that Book of Mormon prophets held the Melchizedek Priesthood.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: That He May Become Strong Also
context: “But this much I can tell you, that if ye do not watch yourselves, and your thoughts, and your words, and your deeds, and observe the commandments of God, and continue in the faith of what ye have heard concerning the coming of our Lord, even unto the end of your lives, ye must perish. And now, O man, remember, and perish not.”

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: That He May Become Strong Also
context: The sons of Helaman did not doubt. They fought bravely and came off conquerors because they believed the words of their mothers.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: That He May Become Strong Also
context: We understand the power of the faith of a loving mother. Mothers provide that great support to their sons today. We holders of the priesthood can and must add to that support with our determination to answer the charge that as we are converted, we are to reach down to strengthen our brethren.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: That He May Become Strong Also
context: “Behold, this is the way that mine apostles, in ancient days, built up my church unto me.”

speaker: Thomas S. Monson
title: Principles and Promises
context: Those who are obedient to the Lord’s commandments and who faithfully observe the Word of Wisdom are promised particular blessings, among which are good health and added physical stamina.

speaker: Thomas S. Monson
title: Principles and Promises
context: John later said that as he finished his prayer, he felt a great surge of strength. He began climbing once again and fairly flew up the rope. When he reached the deck, his breathing was normal and not the least bit labored. The blessings of added health and stamina promised in the Word of Wisdom had been his. He gave thanks to his Heavenly Father then, and throughout the remainder of his life, for the answer to his desperate prayer for help.
footnote_text: See John A. Larsen, in Robert C. Freeman and Dennis A. Wright, comps., Saints at War: Experiences of Latter-day Saints in World War II (2001), 350–51; used by permission.

speaker: Thomas S. Monson
title: The Perfect Path to Happiness
context: We are blessed to have the truth. We have a mandate to share the truth. Let us live the truth, that we might merit all that the Father has for us. He does nothing save it be for our benefit. He has told us, “This is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: These are the latter days, so none of us should be surprised when we see prophecy fulfilled. A host of prophets, including Isaiah, Paul, Nephi, and Mormon, foresaw that perilous times would come,

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: that in our day the whole world would be in commotion,

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: that men would “be lovers of their own selves, … without natural affection, … lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God,”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: and that many would become servants of Satan who uphold the adversary’s work.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: Indeed, you and I “wrestle … against the rulers of the darkness of this world, [and] against spiritual wickedness in high places.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: Clearly, Lehi knew opposition, anxiety, heartache, pain, disappointment, and sorrow. Yet he declared boldly and without reservation a principle as revealed by the Lord: “Men are, that they might have joy.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: Eliza R. Snow, second General President of the Relief Society, offered a riveting answer. Because of Missouri’s infamous extermination order, issued at the onset of the grueling winter of 1838,
footnote_text: Governor Lilburn W. Boggs of Missouri issued the order of Mormon extermination on October 27, 1838 (see Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Joseph Smith [2007], 349).

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: Eliza’s report of that exhausting, bone-chilling evening was strikingly optimistic. She declared: “That was a very merry night. None but saints can be happy under every circumstance.”
footnote_text: See Eliza R. Snow, in Edward W. Tullidge, The Women of Mormondom (1877), 145–46.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: When the focus of our lives is on God’s plan of salvation, which President Thomas S. Monson just taught us, and Jesus Christ and His gospel, we can feel joy regardless of what is happening—or not happening—in our lives. Joy comes from and because of Him. He is the source of all joy. We feel it at Christmastime when we sing, “Joy to the world, the Lord is come.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: That is why our missionaries leave their homes to preach His gospel. Their goal is not to increase the number of Church members. Rather, our missionaries teach and baptize
footnote_text: Missionaries do as the Lord has commanded: they preach, teach, and baptize in His name (see Matthew 28:19; Mark 16:15; Mormon 9:22; Doctrine and Covenants 68:8; 84:62; 112:28). In His Intercessory Prayer, Jesus proclaimed His relationship to the joy of His disciples. He said, “These things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves” (John 17:13; emphasis added).

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: to bring joy to the people of the world!

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: Just as the Savior offers peace that “passeth all understanding,”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: He also offers an intensity, depth, and breadth of joy that defy human logic or mortal comprehension. For example, it doesn’t seem possible to feel joy when your child suffers with an incurable illness or when you lose your job or when your spouse betrays you. Yet that is precisely the joy the Savior offers. His joy is constant, assuring us that our “afflictions shall be but a small moment”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: and be consecrated to our gain.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: How, then, can we claim that joy? We can start by “looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: “in every thought.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: Joy is powerful, and focusing on joy brings God’s power into our lives. As in all things, Jesus Christ is our ultimate exemplar, “who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: A man who frequently demeaned his wife and indulged in angry outbursts at his children focused on the joy of being worthy to have the Holy Ghost as his constant companion. That focus motivated him to put off the natural man,
footnote_text: See Mosiah 3:19. Note: the “natural man” is not only an enemy to God; he is also an enemy to his wife and children.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: A dear colleague recently told me of his past two decades of heavy trials. He said, “I have learned to suffer with joy. My suffering was swallowed up in the joy of Christ.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: What will you and I be able to endure as we focus on the joy that is “set before” us?

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: What repenting will then be possible? What weakness will become a strength?

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: What chastening will become a blessing?

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: What disappointments, even tragedies, will turn to our good?

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: And what challenging service to the Lord will we be able to give?

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: As we diligently focus on the Savior and then follow His pattern of focusing on joy, we need to avoid those things that can interrupt our joy. Remember Korihor, the anti-Christ? Spewing falsehoods about the Savior, Korihor went from place to place until he was brought before a high priest who asked him: “Why do ye go about perverting the ways of the Lord? Why do ye teach this people that there shall be no Christ, to interrupt their rejoicings?”
footnote_text: Alma 30:22. The Book of Mormon is filled with examples of men and women who experience joy and rejoicing because they choose to follow Jesus Christ. Any other choice, as in the case of Korihor, leads to eventual destruction.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: Anything that opposes Christ or His doctrine will interrupt our joy. That includes the philosophies of men, so abundant online and in the blogosphere, which do exactly what Korihor did.
footnote_text: Calumny, meaning a misrepresentation, is defined as a false and malicious statement designed to injure the reputation of someone or something. Calumny was happening in the days of Korihor, and it is happening now. The Prophet Joseph Smith spoke of the invincibility of the Church even in the face of calumny. He said: “The Standard of Truth has been erected; no unhallowed hand can stop the work from progressing; persecutions may rage, mobs may combine, armies may assemble, calumny may defame, but the truth of God will go forth boldly, nobly, and independent, till it has penetrated every continent, visited every clime, swept every country, and sounded in every ear, till the purposes of God shall be accomplished, and the Great Jehovah shall say the work is done” (Teachings: Joseph Smith, 444).

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: If we look to the world and follow its formulas for happiness,
footnote_text: The world teaches that the purchase of things will bring joy. And if that doesn’t work, buy more! It also teaches that you can sin your way to joy. And if that doesn’t work, sin more! The promise is that at the end of every hedonistic rainbow is a pot of joy. Not true!

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: we will never know joy. The unrighteous may experience any number of emotions and sensations, but they will never experience joy!
footnote_text: Not in this world or in the world to come.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: Joy is a gift for the faithful.
footnote_text: Righteous Saints “who have endured the crosses of the world … shall inherit the kingdom of God, … and their joy shall be full forever” (2 Nephi 9:18).

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: It is the gift that comes from intentionally trying to live a righteous life, as taught by Jesus Christ.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: He taught us how to have joy. When we choose Heavenly Father to be our God

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: and when we can feel the Savior’s Atonement working in our lives, we will be filled with joy.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: Heed these words of the Psalmist: “I have set the Lord always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved. … In [His] presence is fulness of joy.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Joy and Spiritual Survival
context: As this principle is embedded in our hearts, each and every day can be a day of joy and gladness.

speaker: Peter F. Meurs
title: The Sacrament Can Help Us Become Holy
context: President Boyd K. Packer taught: “Prelude music, reverently played, is nourishment for the spirit. It invites inspiration.”
footnote_text: Boyd K. Packer, “Personal Revelation: The Gift, the Test, and the Promise,” Ensign, Nov. 1994, 61.

speaker: Peter F. Meurs
title: The Sacrament Can Help Us Become Holy
context: “This is not a time,” President Russell M. Nelson explained, “for conversation or transmission of messages but a period of prayerful meditation as leaders and members prepare spiritually for the sacrament.”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “Worshiping at Sacrament Meeting,” Ensign, Aug. 2004, 27; Liahona, Aug. 2004, 13.

speaker: Peter F. Meurs
title: The Sacrament Can Help Us Become Holy
context: The sacrament hymn is an especially important part of our sacrament experience. Music elevates our thoughts and feelings. The sacrament hymn has even greater influence when we focus on the words and the powerful doctrine taught. We learn much from words such as “Bruised, broken, torn for us,”
footnote_text: “Jesus of Nazareth, Savior and King,” Hymns, no. 181.

speaker: Peter F. Meurs
title: The Sacrament Can Help Us Become Holy
context: “Let us remember and be sure our hearts and hands are clean and pure,”
footnote_text: “While of These Emblems We Partake,” Hymns, no. 173.

speaker: Peter F. Meurs
title: The Sacrament Can Help Us Become Holy
context: and “Where justice, love, and mercy meet in harmony divine!”
footnote_text: “How Great the Wisdom and the Love,” Hymns, no. 195.

speaker: Peter F. Meurs
title: The Sacrament Can Help Us Become Holy
context: As we sing a hymn in preparation to partake of the emblems, the words can become part of our covenant commitment. Consider, for example: “We love thee, Lord; our hearts are full. We’ll walk thy chosen way.”
footnote_text: “As Now We Take the Sacrament,” Hymns, no. 169.

speaker: Peter F. Meurs
title: The Sacrament Can Help Us Become Holy
context: Elder David A. Bednar taught: “The ordinance of the sacrament is a holy and repeated invitation to repent sincerely and to be renewed spiritually. The act of partaking of the sacrament, in and of itself, does not remit sins. But as we prepare conscientiously and participate in this holy ordinance with a broken heart and a contrite spirit, then the promise is that we may always have the Spirit of the Lord to be with us. And by the sanctifying power of the Holy Ghost as our constant companion, we can always retain a remission of our sins.”
footnote_text: David A. Bednar, “Always Retain a Remission of Your Sins,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2016, 61–62.

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: The Great Plan of Redemption
context: Amulek testified, “I would that ye would come forth and harden not your hearts any longer; … if ye will repent … , immediately shall the great plan of redemption be brought about unto you.”

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: The Great Plan of Redemption
context: “… Whatever the cost of repentance, it is swallowed up in the joy of forgiveness.”
footnote_text: D. Todd Christofferson, “The Divine Gift of Repentance,” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2011, 40.

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: The Great Plan of Redemption
context: “And he said unto me: Because of thy faith in Christ. … Go to, thy faith hath made thee whole.”

speaker: Linda S. Reeves
title: The Great Plan of Redemption
context: In a past general conference, Elder Jeffrey R. Holland declared: “However late you think you are, however many chances you think you have missed, however many mistakes you feel you have made … , or however far from home and family and God you feel you have traveled, I testify that you have not traveled beyond the reach of divine love. It is not possible for you to sink lower than the infinite light of Christ’s Atonement shines.”
footnote_text: Jeffrey R. Holland, “The Laborers in the Vineyard,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2012, 33.

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: “That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: One of the most heart-wrenching stories in scripture occurred when “many of [the Lord’s] disciples” found it hard to accept His teachings and doctrine, and they “went back, and walked no more with him.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: As these disciples left, Jesus turned to the Twelve and asked, “Will ye also go away?”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: “And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: Today is no different. For some, Christ’s invitation to believe and remain continues to be hard—or difficult to accept. Some disciples struggle to understand a specific Church policy or teaching. Others find concerns in our history or in the imperfections of some members and leaders, past and present. Still others find it difficult to live a religion that requires so much. Finally, some have become “weary in well-doing.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: Never fail to give equal time to the Lord through honest attempts to understand what the Lord has revealed. As my dear friend and former colleague Elder Neal A. Maxwell once said, “We should not assume … that just because something is unexplainable by us it is unexplainable.”
footnote_text: Neal A. Maxwell, Not My Will, But Thine (1988), 124.

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: Where will you go to be taught about a Savior who is your best friend, who not only suffered for your sins but who also suffered “pains and afflictions and temptations of every kind” so “that his bowels may be filled with mercy, according to the flesh, that he may know according to the flesh how to succor his people according to their infirmities,”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: The danger comes when someone chooses to wander away from the path that leads to the tree of life.

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: In the end, each one of us must respond to the Savior’s question: “Will ye also go away?”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: My sincere hope is that we will invite an increasing number of God’s children to find and stay on the gospel path so they too can “partake of the fruit, which [is] desirable above all other fruit.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: Please know that even though great storms of wind and waves beat upon the old ship, the Savior is on board and is able to rebuke the storm with His command “Peace, be still.” Until then, we must not fear, and we must have unwavering faith and know that “even the wind and the sea obey him.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: “And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: I testify that there is “no other name given nor any other way nor means whereby salvation can come unto the children of men, only in and through the name of Christ.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: I also testify that Jesus Christ has called apostles and prophets in our day and restored His Church with teachings and commandments as “a refuge from the storm, and from wrath” that will surely come unless the people of the world repent and return to Him.

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: To Whom Shall We Go?
context: I further testify that the Lord “inviteth them all to come unto him and partake of his goodness; and he denieth none that come unto him, black and white, bond and free, male and female; … and all are alike unto God.”

speaker: Dean M. Davies
title: The Blessings of Worship
context: One of the most remarkable and tender experiences recorded in holy scripture is the account of the visit of the Savior to people in the Americas following His death and Resurrection. The people had suffered a destruction so great that it caused “the whole earth [to become] deformed.”

speaker: Dean M. Davies
title: The Blessings of Worship
context: The record of those events relates that following the catastrophe, all the people wept continually,

speaker: Dean M. Davies
title: The Blessings of Worship
context: “And behold, I am the light and the life of the world.”

speaker: Dean M. Davies
title: The Blessings of Worship
context: “Hosanna! Blessed be the name of the Most High God!”

speaker: Dean M. Davies
title: The Blessings of Worship
context: And then, for a second time, “they did fall down at the feet of Jesus.” But this time with purpose, for we learn that they “did worship him.”

speaker: Dean M. Davies
title: The Blessings of Worship
context: True disciples are drawn to “worship him that made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the fountains of waters—calling upon the name of the Lord day and night.”

speaker: Dean M. Davies
title: The Blessings of Worship
context: Oliver Cowdery described those days as “never to be forgotten. … What joy! what wonder! what amazement!”

speaker: Dean M. Davies
title: The Blessings of Worship
context: In the Book of Mormon we learn that from the moment Alma the Younger was delivered from suffering the consequences of his own rebelliousness, he was never the same. He boldly “traveled throughout all the land … and among all the people … , zealously striving to repair all the injuries which [he] had done to the church.”

speaker: Dean M. Davies
title: The Blessings of Worship
context: We understand that it is impossible to say that we love God while at the same time hating, dismissing, or disregarding others around us.

speaker: Dean M. Davies
title: The Blessings of Worship
context: We ponder God’s word, and that fills our souls with light and truth. We comprehend spiritual vistas that can be seen only through the light of the Holy Ghost.

speaker: Dean M. Davies
title: The Blessings of Worship
context: “For the Lord is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations.”

speaker: Lynn G. Robbins
title: The Righteous Judge
context: However, compassion doesn’t nullify the need for discipline. The word discipline comes from the Latin word discere, “to learn,” or discipulus, “learner,” making a disciple a student and follower.

speaker: Lynn G. Robbins
title: The Righteous Judge
context: To discipline in the Lord’s way is to lovingly and patiently teach. In the scriptures the Lord often uses the word chasten when speaking of discipline (see, for example, Mosiah 23:21; D&C 95:1). The word chasten comes from the Latin castus, meaning “chaste or pure,” and chasten means “to purify.”

speaker: Lynn G. Robbins
title: The Righteous Judge
context: Young Joseph Smith was disciplined with a four-year probation before obtaining the golden plates, “because you have not kept the commandments of the Lord.”
footnote_text: Karen Lynn Davidson and others, eds., Histories, Volume 1: Joseph Smith Histories, 1832–1844, vol. 1 of the Histories series of The Joseph Smith Papers (2012), 83.

speaker: Lynn G. Robbins
title: The Righteous Judge
context: Joseph said, “The angel was rejoiced when he gave me back the Urim and Thummim and said that God was pleased with my faithfulness and humility, and loved me for my penitence and diligence in prayer.”
footnote_text: Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Joseph Smith (2007), 71; emphasis added.

speaker: Lynn G. Robbins
title: The Righteous Judge
context: “In ancient days, sacrifice meant to make something or someone holy,”

speaker: Lynn G. Robbins
title: The Righteous Judge
context: which links it, in an interdependent way, to the definition of the word chasten—“to purify.” Likewise, in ancient Israel, forgiveness came through a sin or trespass offering, or sacrifice.

speaker: Lynn G. Robbins
title: The Righteous Judge
context: On the other hand, through the sweet irony of sacrifice, we actually gain something of eternal worth—His mercy and forgiveness and eventually “all that [the] Father hath” (D&C 84:38). As part of the repentance process, sacrifice also acts as a healing balm to help replace “remorse of conscience” (Alma 42:18) with “peace of conscience” (Mosiah 4:3). Without sacrifice, a person may find it hard to forgive himself or herself, because of a lingering consciousness of something withheld.
footnote_text: The sacrifice we offer on the altar of the sacrament table each week is a broken heart and a contrite spirit (see 2 Nephi 2:7; 3 Nephi 9:20; Doctrine and Covenants 59:8). A broken heart is a repentant heart; a contrite spirit is an obedient spirit (see D. Todd Christofferson, “When Thou Art Converted,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2004, 12).

speaker: Lynn G. Robbins
title: The Righteous Judge
context: President Joseph F. Smith taught, “If children are defiant and difficult to control, be patient with them until you can conquer by love, … and you can then [mold] their characters as you please.”
footnote_text: Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Joseph F. Smith (1998), 299.

speaker: Lynn G. Robbins
title: The Righteous Judge
context: “… Kindness is the power that God has given us to unlock hard hearts and subdue stubborn souls.”
footnote_text: Teachings of Presidents of the Church: George Albert Smith (2011), 225, 226, 228; emphasis added.

speaker: Lynn G. Robbins
title: The Righteous Judge
context: Perhaps more than opening the mouths of babes, the Lord was opening the eyes and ears of their astonished parents. Those parents had been granted the extraordinary gift of a glimpse into eternity and of beholding the true identity and premortal stature of their children. Would that not forever change the way the parents saw and treated their children? I like this variation of a quote attributed to Goethe: “The way you see [a child] is the way you treat them, and the way you treat them is [who] they [will] become.”
footnote_text: Attributed to Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, brainyquote.com.

speaker: Lynn G. Robbins
title: The Righteous Judge
context: President Thomas S. Monson has taught us, “Never let a problem to be solved become more important than a person to be loved.”
footnote_text: Thomas S. Monson, “Finding Joy in the Journey,” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2008, 86.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Gratitude on the Sabbath Day
context: For Latter-day Saints, the Sabbath is such a moment, actually a day, of gratitude and love. The Lord instructed the Saints in Jackson County, Missouri, in 1831 that their prayers and thanks should be directed heavenward. The early Saints were given a revelation about how to keep the Sabbath day and how to fast and pray.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Gratitude on the Sabbath Day
context: Are you ever burdened with a load of care?Does the cross seem heavy you are called to bear?Count your many blessings; ev’ry doubt will fly,And you will be singing as the days go by.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Gratitude on the Sabbath Day

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Gratitude on the Sabbath Day

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: As the Savior concluded the Sermon on the Mount, He emphasized the eternal truth that “only by doing the will of the Father is the saving grace of the Son obtainable.”
footnote_text: James E. Talmage, Jesus the Christ, 3rd ed. (1916), 245–46.

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: “And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: Our understanding of this episode is enlarged as we reflect upon an inspired revision to the text. Significantly, the Lord’s phrase reported in the King James Version of the Bible, “I never knew you,” was changed in the Joseph Smith Translation to “Ye never knew me.”
footnote_text: Joseph Smith Translation, Matthew 7:33 (in Matthew 7:23, footnote a).

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: “But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: The implications of this parable for each of us are expanded by another inspired revision. Importantly, the phrase “I know you not,” as reported in the King James Version of the Bible, was clarified in the Joseph Smith Translation to “Ye know me not.”
footnote_text: Joseph Smith Translation, Matthew 25:11 (in Matthew 25:12, footnote a).

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: “If ye had known me, ye should have known my Father also.”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: We begin to come to know the Savior as we arouse our spiritual faculties and experiment upon His teachings, even until we can give place in our souls for a portion of His words.

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: True faith is focused in and on the Lord and always leads to righteous action. “Faith [in Christ is] the first principle in revealed religion, … the foundation of all righteousness, … and the principle of action in all intelligent beings.”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: Because acting in accordance with the correct principles the Redeemer proclaimed is central to receiving and exercising true faith, “faith without works is dead.”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: We are to be “doers of the word, and not hearers only.”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: Hearing God’s word and receiving the spiritual gift of faith in the Savior are closely related, as “faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: We become acquainted with Him and His voice as we study and feast upon His word in the scriptures,

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”

footnote_text: See John 7:17. Each of us has a responsibility to seek after and do all that we can do to qualify for the gift of faith. Ultimately, however, a loving and caring God bestows the gift upon us.

title: “If Ye Had Known Me”

footnote_text: See Joseph Smith Translation, Matthew 16:26 (in the Bible appendix).

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: The Savior has admonished us to become as He is.

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: In His mortal ministry, Jesus marked the path, led the way, and set the perfect example. “A correct idea of his character, perfections, and attributes”

title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: Following the Savior also enables us to receive “an actual knowledge that the course of life [we are] pursuing”

title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: Lehi’s dream in the Book of Mormon identifies the path we should follow, the challenges we will encounter, and the spiritual resources available to assist us in following and coming unto the Savior. Pressing forward on the strait and narrow path is what He would have us do. Tasting the fruit of the tree and becoming deeply “converted unto the Lord”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: are the blessings He yearns for us to receive. Hence, He beckons us, “Come, follow me.”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: “For how knoweth a man the master whom he has not served, and who is a stranger unto him, and is far from the thoughts and intents of his heart?”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: He declared: “For I will go before your face. I will be on your right hand and on your left, and my Spirit shall be in your hearts, and mine angels round about you, to bear you up.”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: We come to know the Savior as we do our best to go where He wants us to go, as we strive to say what He wants us to say, and as we become what He wants us to become.
footnote_text: See “I’ll Go Where You Want Me to Go,” Hymns, no. 270.

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: As we submissively acknowledge our total dependence upon Him, He enlarges our capacity to serve ever more effectively. Gradually, our desires align more completely with His desires, and His purposes become our purposes, such that we would “not ask that which is contrary to [His] will.”

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: Serving Him requires all of our heart, might, mind, and strength.

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: Consequently, selflessly serving others counteracts the self-centered and selfish tendencies of the natural man. We grow to love those whom we serve. And because serving others is serving God, we grow to love Him and our brothers and sisters more deeply. Such love is a manifestation of the spiritual gift of charity, even the pure love of Christ.

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: “Pray unto the Father with all the energy of heart, that ye may be filled with this love, which he hath bestowed upon all who are true followers of his Son, Jesus Christ; that ye may become the sons of God; that when he shall appear we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is; that we may have this hope; that we may be purified even as he is pure.”

context: We believe and come to know the Lord as the key of the knowledge of God administered through the Melchizedek Priesthood unlocks the door and makes it possible for each of us to receive the power of godliness in our lives. We believe and come to know the Savior as we follow Him by receiving and faithfully honoring holy ordinances and increasingly have His image in our countenances.

speaker: David A. Bednar
title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: We believe and come to know Christ as we experience personally the transforming, healing, strengthening, and sanctifying power of His Atonement. We believe and come to know the Master as “the power of his word [takes root] in us”

title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
context: and is written in our minds and hearts

title: “If Ye Had Known Me”

title: “If Ye Had Known Me”
