footnote_text: For a more in-depth look at this period of history, see Saints: The Story of the Church of Jesus Christ in the Latter Days, vol. 2, No Unhallowed Hand, 1846–1893 (2020), chapters 17, 19, and 21.

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: God Will Do Something Unimaginable
context: Finally, the Saints could sing the hymn “How Firm a Foundation”
footnote_text: See “How Firm a Foundation,” Hymns, no. 85. The verses of this great anthem can serve as a theme for our times, and when we listen to the lyrics with new ears, it provides insight into the challenges we face: In ev’ry condition—in sickness, in health, In poverty’s vale or abounding in wealth, At home or abroad, on the land or the sea— As thy days may demand, … so thy succor shall be. Fear not, I am with thee; oh, be not dismayed, For I am thy God and will still give thee aid. I’ll strengthen thee, help thee, and cause thee to stand, Upheld by my righteous, … omnipotent hand. When through the deep waters I call thee to go, The rivers of sorrow shall not thee o’erflow, For I will be with thee, thy troubles to bless, And sanctify to thee … thy deepest distress. When through fiery trials thy pathway shall lie, My grace, all sufficient, shall be thy supply. The flame shall not hurt thee; I only design Thy dross to consume … and thy gold to refine. … The soul that on Jesus hath leaned for repose I will not, I cannot, desert to his foes; That soul, though all hell should endeavor to shake, I’ll never, no never, … no never forsake!

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: God Will Do Something Unimaginable
context: Enoch and his people lived in a time of wickedness, wars, and bloodshed. “But the Lord came and dwelt with his people.” He had something unimaginable in mind for them. He helped them establish Zion—a people “of one heart and one mind” who “dwelt in righteousness.”

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: God Will Do Something Unimaginable
context: Young Joseph, the son of Jacob, was thrown into a pit, sold into slavery, betrayed, and abandoned.
footnote_text: Joseph was perhaps as young as 17 when his brothers sold him into slavery (see Genesis 37:2). He was 30 years old when he entered Pharaoh’s service (see Genesis 41:46). Can you imagine how difficult it was for a young man in his prime to be betrayed, sold into slavery, falsely accused, and then imprisoned? Joseph certainly is a model for not only the youth of the Church but also every man, woman, and child who desires to take up the cross and follow the Savior.

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: God Will Do Something Unimaginable
context: Joseph must have wondered if God had forgotten him. God had something unimaginable in mind for Joseph. He used this period of trial to strengthen Joseph’s character and put him in a position to save his family.
footnote_text: See Genesis 45:4–11; 50:20–21. In Psalm 105:17–18, we read, “He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant: whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron.” In another translation, verse 18 reads, “They have afflicted with fetters his feet, Iron hath entered his soul” (Young’s Literal Translation). To me, this suggests that Joseph’s hardships gave him a soul as strong and resilient as iron—a quality he would need for the great and unimaginable future the Lord had in store for him.

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: God Will Do Something Unimaginable
context: Think of Joseph Smith the Prophet while imprisoned in Liberty Jail, how he pled for relief for the suffering Saints. He must have wondered how Zion could be established in those circumstances. But the Lord spoke peace to him, and the glorious revelation that followed brought peace to the Saints—and it continues to bring peace to you and me.

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: God Will Do Something Unimaginable
context: Second, our Heavenly Father knows that we suffer, and because we are His children, He will not abandon us.
footnote_text: If God commands His children to be aware of and compassionate toward the hungry, the needy, the naked, the sick, and the afflicted, surely He will be aware of and merciful to us, His children (see Mormon 8:39).

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: God Will Do Something Unimaginable
context: Think of the compassionate one, the Savior, who spent so much of His life ministering to the sick, the lonely, the doubting, the despairing.

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: God Will Do Something Unimaginable
context: They did cast their nets on the other side and “were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes.”

speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
title: God Will Do Something Unimaginable
context: As an Apostle of the Lord, I invite and bless you to “cheerfully do all things that lie in [your] power; and then may [you] stand still, with the utmost assurance, to see the salvation of God, and for his arm to be revealed.”

speaker: Sharon Eubank
title: By Union of Feeling We Obtain Power with God
context: On June 9, the Prophet “said he was going to preach mercy[.] Supposing that Jesus Christ and [the] angels should object to us on frivolous things, what would become of us? We must be merciful and overlook small things.” President Smith continued, “It grieves me that there is no fuller fellowship—if one member suffer all feel it—by union of feeling we obtain pow’r with God.”
footnote_text: “Minutes and Discourse, 9 June 1842,” 61, Joseph Smith Papers, josephsmithpapers.org/paper-summary/minutes-and-discourse-9-june-1842/1.

speaker: Sharon Eubank
title: By Union of Feeling We Obtain Power with God
context: “… The nearer we get to our heavenly Father, the more are we dispos’d to look with compassion on perishing souls—[we feel that we want] to take them upon our shoulders and cast their sins behind our back. [My talk is intended for] all this Society—if you would have God have mercy on you, have mercy on one another.”
footnote_text: “Minutes and Discourse, 9 June 1842,” 62, Joseph Smith Papers, josephsmithpapers.org/paper-summary/minutes-and-discourse-9-june-1842/2.

speaker: Sharon Eubank
title: By Union of Feeling We Obtain Power with God
context: This was counsel specifically to the Relief Society. Let’s not judge each other or let our words bite. Let’s keep each other’s names safe and give the gift of mercy.
footnote_text: See Cree-L Kofford, “Your Name Is Safe in Our Home,” Ensign, May 1999, 81–83; Liahona, July 1999, 96–98.

speaker: Sharon Eubank
title: By Union of Feeling We Obtain Power with God
context: Differences can be turned to advantage instead of disadvantage. Only then will it feel as if the boat is moving on its own. Only then does pain entirely give way to exultation. Good “swing” feels like poetry.
footnote_text: See Daniel James Brown, The Boys in the Boat: Nine Americans and Their Epic Quest for Gold at the 1936 Berlin Olympics (2013), 161, 179.

speaker: Sharon Eubank
title: By Union of Feeling We Obtain Power with God
context: The servant says to the Lord of the vineyard: “Spare [the tree] a little longer. And the Lord said: Yea, I will spare it a little longer.”

speaker: Sharon Eubank
title: By Union of Feeling We Obtain Power with God
context: And then comes instruction that can be applied to all of us trying to dig about and find good fruit in our own little vineyards: “Ye shall clear away the bad according as the good shall grow.”

speaker: Sharon Eubank
title: By Union of Feeling We Obtain Power with God
context: We are never alone in our efforts to create unity. Jacob 5 continues, “The servants did go and labor with their mights; and the Lord of the vineyard labored also with them.”

speaker: Sharon Eubank
title: By Union of Feeling We Obtain Power with God
context: Jesus put it bluntly: “Be one; and if ye are not one ye are not mine.”

speaker: Sharon Eubank
title: By Union of Feeling We Obtain Power with God
context: We may not yet be where we want to be, and we are not now where we will be. I believe the change we seek in ourselves and in the groups we belong to will come less by activism and more by actively trying every day to understand one another. Why? Because we are building Zion—a people “of one heart and one mind.”

speaker: Sharon Eubank
title: By Union of Feeling We Obtain Power with God
context: When the Church commemorated the 1978 revelation on priesthood, President Russell M. Nelson extended a powerful prophetic blessing: “It is my prayer and blessing that I leave upon all who are listening that we may overcome any burdens of prejudice and walk uprightly with God—and with one another—in perfect peace and harmony.”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “Building Bridges,” New Era, Aug. 2018, 6; Liahona, Dec. 2018, 51; emphasis added.

speaker: Sharon Eubank
title: By Union of Feeling We Obtain Power with God
context: May we draw on this prophetic blessing and use our individual and collective efforts to increase unity in the world. I leave my testimony in the words of the Lord Jesus Christ’s humble, timeless prayer: “That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us.”

speaker: Becky Craven
title: Keep the Change
context: King Benjamin taught his people in ancient America of the tremendous blessings we receive from our Savior, Jesus Christ. He created the heavens, the earth, and all the beauty we enjoy.

speaker: Becky Craven
title: Keep the Change
context: Through His loving Atonement, He provides a way for us to be redeemed from sin and death.

speaker: Becky Craven
title: Keep the Change
context: After hearing the words spoken by King Benjamin, his people cried out, declaring that their hearts had changed, saying, “Because of the Spirit of the Lord Omnipotent, which has wrought a mighty change in us, … we have no more disposition to do evil, but to do good continually.”

speaker: Becky Craven
title: Keep the Change
context: President Henry B. Eyring teaches: “True conversion depends on seeking freely in faith, with great effort and some pain. Then it is the Lord who can grant … the miracle of cleansing and change.”
footnote_text: Henry B. Eyring, “We Must Raise Our Sights,” Ensign, Sept. 2004, 18.

speaker: Becky Craven
title: Keep the Change
context: When I was younger, I visualized myself walking along an upward, vertical path toward my goal of eternal life. Each time I did or said something wrong, I felt myself sliding down the path, only to start my journey all over again. It was like landing on that one square in the children’s game Chutes and Ladders that slides you down from the top of the board back to the beginning of the game! It was discouraging! But as I began to understand the doctrine of Christ

speaker: Becky Craven
title: Keep the Change
context: Jesus Christ has given us a continuous pattern for change. He invites us to exercise faith in Him, which inspires us to repent—“which faith and repentance bringeth a change of heart.”

speaker: Becky Craven
title: Keep the Change
context: There is an inspired phrase in the Young Women theme that states, “I cherish the gift of repentance and seek to improve each day.”

speaker: Cristina B. Franco
title: The Healing Power of Jesus Christ
context: President Russell M. Nelson taught: “When sore trials come upon us, it’s time to deepen our faith in God, to work hard, and to serve others. Then He will heal our broken hearts. He will bestow upon us personal peace and comfort. Those great gifts will not be destroyed, even by death.”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “Jesus Christ—the Master Healer,” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2005, 87.

speaker: Cristina B. Franco
title: The Healing Power of Jesus Christ
context: To heal brokenness by coming unto Him, we need to have faith in Jesus Christ. “Having faith in Jesus Christ means relying completely on Him—trusting in His infinite power … and love. It includes believing His teachings. It means believing that even though we do not understand all things, He does. Because He has experienced all our pains, afflictions, and infirmities, He knows how to help us rise above our daily difficulties.”
footnote_text: “Faith in Jesus Christ,” Gospel Topics, topics.ChurchofJesusChrist.org.

speaker: Cristina B. Franco
title: The Healing Power of Jesus Christ
context: As we come unto Him, “we can be filled with joy, peace, and consolation. All that is [hard and challenging] about life can be made right through the Atonement of Jesus Christ.”
footnote_text: Preach My Gospel: A Guide to Missionary Service, rev. ed. (2018), 52, ChurchofJesusChrist.org.

speaker: Cristina B. Franco
title: The Healing Power of Jesus Christ
context: “Oh, what hope soars in those promises! … His spirit heals; it refines; it comforts; it breathes new life into hopeless hearts. It has the power to transform all that is ugly and vicious and worthless in life to something of supreme and glorious splendor. He has the power to convert the ashes of mortality to the beauties of eternity.”
footnote_text: Tad R. Callister, The Infinite Atonement (2000), 206–7.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Sisters in Zion
context: As the beloved daughters of Heavenly Father, and as the daughters of the Lord Jesus Christ in His kingdom,

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Sisters in Zion
context: “And there shall be mine abode, and it shall be Zion, which shall come forth out of all the creations which I have made; and for the space of a thousand years the earth shall rest.”

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Sisters in Zion
context: The Lord has, through His prophets, made a promise to you. In the early days of the Relief Society, the Prophet Joseph Smith said to the sisters, “If you live up to your privileges, the angels cannot be restrained from being your associates.”
footnote_text: Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Joseph Smith (2007), 454; emphasis added.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Sisters in Zion
context: “Each of you is a daughter of God, endowed with a divine birthright.”
footnote_text: Gordon B. Hinckley, “Women of the Church,” Ensign, Nov. 1996, 67.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Sisters in Zion
context: “This has been true in every gospel dispensation since the days of Adam and Eve. Yet the women of this dispensation are distinct from the women of any other because this dispensation is distinct from any other. This distinction brings both privileges and responsibilities.”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “A Plea to My Sisters,” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2015, 95–96; emphasis added.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Sisters in Zion
context: “This same Zion which was taken up into heaven shall return … when the Lord brings again Zion, and its inhabitants shall join with the new Jerusalem, which shall then be established.”
footnote_text: Bruce R. McConkie, “Building Zion,” Tambuli, Sept. 1977, 13; emphasis added.

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Sisters in Zion
context: I will tell you why I believe that will be so. The Book of Mormon gives an account of a Zion people. You remember that it was after they had been taught, loved, and blessed by the resurrected Savior that “there was no contention in the land, because of the love of God which did dwell in the hearts of the people.”

speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
title: Be of Good Cheer
context: In the final days of His mortal life, Jesus Christ told His Apostles of the persecutions and hardships they would suffer.

speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
title: Be of Good Cheer
context: Tribulation and challenges are the common experiences of mortality. Opposition is an essential part of the divine plan for helping us grow,

speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
title: Be of Good Cheer
context: and in the midst of that process, we have God’s assurance that, in the long view of eternity, opposition will not be allowed to overcome us. With His help and our faithfulness and endurance, we will prevail. Like the mortal life of which they are a part, all tribulations are temporary. In the controversies that preceded a disastrous war, United States president Abraham Lincoln wisely reminded his audience of the ancient wisdom that “this, too, shall pass away.”
footnote_text: Abraham Lincoln, address to the Wisconsin State Agricultural Society, Milwaukee, Sept. 30, 1859, in John Bartlett, Bartlett’s Familiar Quotations, 18th ed. (2012), 444.

speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
title: Be of Good Cheer
context: Yet, in the midst of all of this, we have that heavenly counsel to be of good cheer and to find joy in the principles and promises of the gospel and the fruits of our labors.

speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
title: Be of Good Cheer
context: Think of those early members! Again and again, they were driven from place to place. Finally they faced the challenges of establishing their homes and the Church in a wilderness.
footnote_text: See Lawrence E. Corbridge, “Surviving and Thriving like the Pioneers,” Ensign, July 2020, 23–24.

speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
title: Be of Good Cheer
context: Even though the Saints were not settled in their new homes, at October 1849 general conference a new wave of missionaries was sent out to Scandinavia, France, Germany, Italy, and the South Pacific.
footnote_text: See “Minutes of the General Conference of 6 October 1849,” General Church Minutes Collection, Church History Library, Salt Lake City.

speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
title: Be of Good Cheer
context: At what could have been thought their lowest level, the pioneers rose to new heights. And just three years later, another 98 were also called to begin to gather scattered Israel. One of the Church leaders explained that these missions “are generally, not to be very long ones; probably from 3 to 7 years will be as long as any man will be absent from his family.”
footnote_text: George A. Smith, in Journal History of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Aug. 28, 1852, 1, Church History Library, Salt Lake City.

speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
title: Be of Good Cheer
context: “You may be facing overwhelming challenges,” Elder Richard G. Scott taught. “Sometimes they are so concentrated, so unrelenting, that you may feel they are beyond your capacity to control. Don’t face the world alone. ‘Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding’ [Proverbs 3:5]. … It was intended that life be a challenge, not so that you would fail, but that you might succeed through overcoming.”
footnote_text: Richard G. Scott, Finding Peace, Happiness, and Joy (2007), 248–49.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: You embody the hopes that President Gordon B. Hinckley had for you when he introduced “The Family: A Proclamation to the World” 25 years ago in the September 1995 general Relief Society meeting.
footnote_text: See “The Family: A Proclamation to the World,” ChurchofJesusChrist.org. In the address that accompanied this proclamation, President Gordon B. Hinckley said to the sisters: “I am grateful for the strength that you have and for your loyalty, your faith, your love. I am thankful for the resolution which you carry in your hearts to walk in faith, to keep the commandments, to do what is right at all times and in all circumstances” (“Stand Strong against the Wiles of the World,” Ensign, Nov. 1995, 98–99).

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: Admittedly, the Lord has spoken of our day in sobering terms. He warned that in our day “men’s hearts [would fail] them”
footnote_text: Luke 21:26; see also Doctrine and Covenants 45:26.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: and that even the very elect would be at risk of being deceived.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: He told the Prophet Joseph Smith that “peace [would] be taken from the earth”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: and calamities would befall mankind.
footnote_text: See Doctrine and Covenants 1:17. The Apostle Paul prophesied that “in the last days perilous times [would] come.” That would make our day spiritually treacherous. (See 2 Timothy 3:1–5.)

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: Yet the Lord has also provided a vision of how remarkable this dispensation is. He inspired the Prophet Joseph Smith to declare that “the work of … these last days, is one of vast magnitude. … Its glories are past description, and its grandeur unsurpassable.”
footnote_text: Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Joseph Smith (2007), 512.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: Now, grandeur may not be the word you would choose to describe these past few months! How are we to deal with both the somber prophecies and the glorious pronouncements about our day? The Lord told us how with simple, but stunning, reassurance: “If ye are prepared ye shall not fear.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: First, he helped them create areas where they would be safe—“places of security” he called them.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: Second, he prepared “the minds of the people to be faithful unto the Lord.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: And third, he never stopped preparing his people—physically or spiritually.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: Moroni fortified every Nephite city with embankments, forts, and walls.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: When the Lamanites came against them, they “were astonished exceedingly, because of the wisdom of the Nephites in preparing their places of security.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: Likewise, the stakes of Zion are “a refuge from the storm”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: The temple—the house of the Lord—is a place of security unlike any other. There, you sisters are endowed with priesthood power through the sacred priesthood covenants you make.
footnote_text: See Russell M. Nelson, “Spiritual Treasures,” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2019, 76–79.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: Simply said, a place of security is anywhere you can feel the presence of the Holy Ghost and be guided by Him.
footnote_text: Eliza R. Snow taught that the Holy Ghost “satisfies and fills up every longing of the human heart. … When I am filled with that Spirit, my soul is satisfied, and I can say in good earnest, that the trifling things of the day do not seem to stand in my way at all. … Is it not our privilege to so live that we can have this constantly flowing into our souls?” (in Daughters in My Kingdom: The History and Work of Relief Society [2011], 46).

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: Some questioned the need for taking such extraordinary measures. However, when the Salt Lake Valley suffered a 5.7-magnitude earthquake earlier this year, this venerable temple shook hard enough that the trumpet on the statue of the angel Moroni fell!
footnote_text: See Daniel Burke, “Utah Earthquake Damages Mormon Temple and Knocks Trumpet from Iconic Angel Statue,” Mar. 18, 2020, cnn.com.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: Just as the physical foundation of the Salt Lake Temple must be strong enough to withstand natural disasters, our spiritual foundations must be solid. Then, when metaphorical earthquakes rock our lives, we can stand “steadfast and immovable” because of our faith.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: The Lord taught us how to increase our faith by seeking “learning, even by study and also by faith.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: We strengthen our faith in Jesus Christ as we strive to keep His commandments and “always remember him.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: The Lord has promised that if we will ask, we may receive “revelation upon revelation.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: Dear sisters, you are adept at creating places of security for yourselves and those you love. Further, you have a divine endowment that enables you to build faith in others in compelling ways.
footnote_text: The Apostle Paul signaled this reality when he attributed Timothy’s unfeigned faith to his mother, Eunice, and his grandmother Lois (see 2 Timothy 1:5).

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Embrace the Future with Faith
context: I promise that as we create places of security, prepare our minds to be faithful to God, and never stop preparing, God will bless us. He will “deliver us; yea, insomuch that he [will] speak peace to our souls, and [will] grant unto us great faith, and … cause us that we [can] hope for our deliverance in him.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: My dear brothers and sisters, during the last week of His mortal ministry, Jesus taught His disciples to “watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: Among the “things that shall come to pass” before His Second Coming are “wars and rumours of wars[,] … famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: In the Doctrine and Covenants, the Savior said, “And all things shall be in commotion; … for fear shall come upon all people.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: On Sunday, October 20, I spoke to a large gathering near Boston, Massachusetts. As I was speaking, I was prompted to say, “I plead with you … to pray for this country, for our leaders, for our people, and for the families that live in this great nation founded by God.”
footnote_text: M. Russell Ballard, in Sarah Jane Weaver, “President Ballard Pleads with Latter-day Saints to ‘Pray for This Country’ as United States Is at ‘Another Crossroad,’” Church News, Oct. 21, 2019, thechurchnews.com.

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: I also said that America and many of the nations of the earth, as in times past, are at another critical crossroads and need our prayers.
footnote_text: See Weaver, “President Ballard Pleads with Latter-day Saints.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: “And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.”
footnote_text: Matthew 6:9–13. Notice that the Joseph Smith Translation clarifies verse 13: “And suffer [permit] us not to be led into temptation, but deliver us from evil” (Joseph Smith Translation, Matthew 6:14 [in Matthew 6:13, footnote a]).

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: I invite you to pray always.

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: The Savior taught us to not limit who we pray for. He said, “Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: On the cross of Calvary, where Jesus died for our sins, He practiced what He taught when He prayed, “Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: Praying for justice, peace, the poor, and the sick is often not enough. After we kneel in prayer, we need to get up from our knees and do what we can to help—to help both ourselves and others.

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: The scriptures are full of examples of people of faith who combined prayer with action to make a difference in their own lives and in the lives of others. In the Book of Mormon, for example, we read about Enos. It has been observed that “about two-thirds of his short book describes a prayer or series of prayers, and the balance tells what he did in consequence of the answers he received.”
footnote_text: Sharon J. Harris, Enos, Jarom, Omni: A Brief Theological Introduction (2020), 18.

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: Brothers and sisters, I urge you to redouble your commitment to prayer. I urge you to pray in your closets, in your daily walk, in your homes, in your wards, and always in your hearts.

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: The Savior prayed and then He “went about doing good”

speaker: M. Russell Ballard
title: Watch Ye Therefore, and Pray Always
context: I invite all Church members, as well as our neighbors and friends of other faith groups worldwide, to do as the Savior counseled His disciples: “Watch ye therefore, and pray always”
footnote_text: Luke 21:36, emphasis added; see also 3 Nephi 18:15.

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: Such an event happened with Jesus’s disciples during His mortal ministry. In Mark we read that Jesus “began again to teach by the sea side: and there was gathered unto him a great multitude.”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: The crowd became so numerous that Jesus “entered into a ship”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: “And … when the [evening] was come,” He said unto His disciples, “Let us pass over unto the other side. And when they had sent away the multitude,”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: they departed from the shore and were on their way across the Sea of Galilee. Finding a spot in the back of the ship, Jesus lay down and quickly fell asleep. Soon “there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was [nearly] full”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: “Master, carest thou not that we perish?”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: “Lord, save us: we perish.”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: They called Him “Master,” and that He is. He is also “Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Father of heaven and earth, the Creator of all things from the beginning.”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: From His position in the boat, Jesus arose and rebuked the wind and said unto the raging sea, “Peace, be still. And the wind [did cease], and there was a great calm.”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: “Why are ye so fearful?”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: “Where is your faith?”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: There is a mortal tendency, even a temptation, when we find ourselves in the middle of trials, troubles, or afflictions to cry out, “Master, carest thou not that I perish? Save me.” Even Joseph Smith pleaded from an awful prison, “O God, where art thou? And where is the pavilion that covereth thy hiding place?”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: To those with proven faith, childlike faith, or even the smallest particle of faith,

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: Jesus invites, saying: “Come unto me.”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: “Believe on my name.”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: “Learn of me, and listen to my words.”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: He tenderly commands, “Repent and [be] baptized in my name,”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: “Love one another; as I have loved you,”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: and “Always remember me.”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: Jesus reassures, explaining: “These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: Regardless of our circumstances, we can intentionally make efforts to build and increase our faith in Jesus Christ. It is strengthened when we remember that we are children of God and that He loves us. Our faith grows as we experiment on the word of God with hope and diligence, trying our very best to follow Christ’s teachings. Our faith increases as we choose to believe rather than doubt, forgive rather than judge, repent rather than rebel. Our faith is refined as we patiently rely on the merits and mercy and grace of the Holy Messiah.

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: “While faith is not a perfect knowledge,” Elder Neal A. Maxwell said, “it brings a deep trust in God, whose knowledge is perfect!”
footnote_text: Neal A. Maxwell, “Lest Ye Be Wearied and Faint in Your Minds,” Ensign, May 1991, 89.

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: Even in turbulent times, faith in the Lord Jesus Christ is gritty and resilient. It helps us sift through unimportant distractions. It encourages us to keep moving along the covenant path. Faith pushes through discouragement and allows us to face the future with resolve and squared shoulders. It prompts us to ask for rescue and relief as we pray to the Father in the name of His Son. And when prayerful pleas seem to go unanswered, our persistent faith in Jesus Christ produces patience, humility, and the ability to reverently utter the words “Thy will be done.”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: “Start with your children. … Let them feel your faith, even when sore trials come upon you. Let your faith be focused on our loving Heavenly Father and His Beloved Son, the Lord Jesus Christ. … Teach each precious boy or girl that he or she is a child of God, created in His image, with a sacred purpose and potential. Each is born with challenges to overcome and faith to be developed.”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “Face the Future with Faith,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2011, 34.

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: Jesus declared, “Therefore, whoso repenteth and cometh unto me as a little child, him will I receive, for of such is the kingdom of God.”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: “For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.”

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: Recently, President Nelson promised “that decreased fear and increased faith will follow” as we “begin anew truly to hear, hearken to, and heed the words of the Savior.”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “Go Forward in Faith,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2020, 114.

speaker: Lisa L. Harkness
title: Peace, Be Still
context: Sisters and brothers, our current challenging circumstances are not our final, eternal destination. As members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, we have taken upon us the name of Jesus Christ by covenant. We have faith in His redeeming power and hope in His great and precious promises. We have every reason to rejoice, for our Lord and Savior is keenly aware of our troubles, cares, and sorrows. As Jesus was with His disciples of old, He is in our boat! I testify He has given His life so that you and I will not perish. May we trust Him, obey His commandments, and with faith hear Him say, “Peace, be still.”

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: “Thou compassest my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways.”

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: In this poem’s semantic parallelism, the Psalmist praises the Lord’s divine attribute of omniscience because He truly knows every aspect of our souls.
footnote_text: See Guide to the Scriptures, “Omniscient,” scriptures.ChurchofJesusChrist.org; see also Matthew 6:8; 2 Nephi 2:24; 3 Nephi 28:6; Doctrine and Covenants 6:16.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: Being aware of all that is necessary for us in this life, the Savior invites us to seek Him in every thought and to follow Him with all our heart.
footnote_text: See Psalm 119:2; Isaiah 45:22; Mosiah 7:33; Doctrine and Covenants 6:36.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: This gives us the promise that we can walk in His light and that His guidance prevents the influence of darkness in our life.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: Seeking Christ in every thought and following Him with all our heart requires that we align our mind and desires with His.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: The scriptures refer to this alignment as “stand[ing] fast in the Lord.”

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: This course of action implies that we continually conduct our lives in harmony with the gospel of Christ and focus daily on everything that is good.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: Only then may we achieve “the peace of God, which passeth all understanding” and which will “keep [our] hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.”

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: The Savior Himself instructed the elders of the Church in February 1831, “Treasure these things up in your hearts, and let the solemnities of eternity rest upon your minds.”

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: Despite our continuous efforts to seek out the Lord, inappropriate thoughts may penetrate our mind. When such thoughts are permitted and even invited to stay, they can shape the desires of our heart and lead us to what we will become in this life and eventually to what we will inherit for eternity.
footnote_text: See Proverbs 23:7; Jeremiah 17:10; 2 Nephi 9:39; Mosiah 4:30; Alma 12:14; Doctrine and Covenants 137:9.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: Elder Neal A. Maxwell once emphasized this principle by saying, “Desires … determine the gradations in outcomes, including why ‘many are called, but few are chosen.’”
footnote_text: Neal A. Maxwell, “According to the Desire of [Our] Hearts,” Ensign, Nov. 1996, 22; see also Matthew 22:14; Doctrine and Covenants 95:5.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: When Moroni called upon the people to believe in Christ and to repent, he urged them to come unto the Savior with all their hearts, stripping themselves from all uncleanness. Furthermore, Moroni invited them to ask God, with unbreakable determination, that they would not fall into temptation.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: “The Holy Ghost shall be thy constant companion, and thy scepter an unchanging scepter of righteousness and truth.”

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: Moroni also reminded his people not to be consumed by their lusts.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: The word lust refers to an intense longing and improper desire for something.
footnote_text: See Guide to the Scriptures, “Lust,” scriptures.ChurchofJesusChrist.org.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: It encompasses any dark thoughts or evil desires that cause an individual to focus on selfish practices or worldly possessions rather than doing good, being kind, keeping the commandments of God, and so forth. It is often manifested through the most carnal feelings of the soul. The Apostle Paul identified some of these feelings, such as “uncleanness, lasciviousness, … hatred, … wrath, strife, … envyings, … and such like.”

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: Fortunately, like the prodigal son in the famous parable found in the gospel of Luke, “he came to himself” and woke up from that nightmare.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: My dear friends, when we resist the little temptations, which often come unexpectedly in our life, we are better equipped to avoid serious transgressions. As President Spencer W. Kimball said: “Seldom does one enter into deeper transgression without first yielding to lesser ones, which open the door to the greater. … ‘A clean field [does not] suddenly [become] weedy.’”
footnote_text: Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Spencer W. Kimball (2006), 106; see also 2 Samuel 11.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: While preparing to accomplish His divine mission on earth, the Savior Jesus Christ exemplified the importance of constantly resisting everything that might dissuade us from realizing our eternal purpose. After several unsuccessful attacks by the enemy, who attempted to divert Him from His mission, the Savior categorically dismissed the devil by saying: “Get thee hence, Satan. … Then the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him.”

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: In his historic and touching message from April this year, our dear prophet, President Russell M. Nelson, made a promise that all those who are willing to “hear Him”—hear Jesus Christ—and obey His commandments “will be blessed with additional power to deal with temptation, struggles, and weakness” and that our capacity to feel joy will increase, even during the increasing current turbulence.
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “Hear Him,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2020, 90.

speaker: Ulisses Soares
title: Seek Christ in Every Thought
context: I testify to you that the promises given by our dear prophet are the promises given by the Savior Himself. I invite all of us to “hear Him” in every thought and follow Him with all our heart in order to obtain the strength and courage to say, “No” and “Get thee hence” to all the things that might bring unhappiness into our life. If we do so, I promise that the Lord will send an added measure of His Holy Spirit to strengthen and comfort us and we may become individuals after the Lord’s own heart.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: During this period of uncertainty, I have felt an unusual gratitude for my sure and certain knowledge that Jesus is the Christ. Have you felt that way? There are difficulties that weigh upon each of us, but always before us is He who humbly declared, “I am the way, the truth, and the life.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: While we endure a season of physically distancing ourselves from others, we need never endure a season of spiritually distancing ourselves from Him who lovingly calls to us, “Come unto me.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: Interestingly, while this spiritual conviction is increasing within us, there are many on the earth who know very little of Jesus Christ, and in some parts of the world where His name has been proclaimed for centuries, faith in Jesus Christ is diminishing. The valiant Saints in Europe have seen belief decline in their countries through the decades.
footnote_text: See Niztan Peri-Rotem, “Religion and Fertility in Western Europe: Trends across Cohorts in Britain, France and the Netherlands,” European Journal of Population, May 2016, 231–65, ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4875064.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: Sadly, here in the United States faith is also receding. A recent study revealed that in the last 10 years, 30 million people in the United States have stepped away from believing in the divinity of Jesus Christ.
footnote_text: “[Sixty-five percent] of American adults describe themselves as Christians when asked about their religion, down 12 percentage points over the past decade. Meanwhile, the religiously unaffiliated share of the population, consisting of people who describe their religious identity as atheist, agnostic or ‘nothing in particular,’ now stands at 26%, up from 17% in 2009” (Pew Research Center, “In U.S., Decline of Christianity Continues at Rapid Pace,” Oct. 17, 2019, pewforum.org).

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: Looking worldwide, another study predicts that in the decades ahead, more than twice as many will leave Christianity as will embrace it.
footnote_text: See Pew Research Center, “The Future of World Religions: Population Growth Projections, 2010–2050,” Apr. 2, 2015, pewforum.org.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: We, of course, revere the right of each to choose, yet our Heavenly Father declared, “This is my beloved Son: hear him.”
footnote_text: Mark 9:7; Luke 9:35; see also Matthew 3:17; Joseph Smith—History 1:17.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: I witness that the day will come when every knee will bow and every tongue confess that Jesus is the Christ.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: Part of our answer may come as we remember how the Lord tutored President Russell M. Nelson in the months prior to his call as President of the Church. Speaking one year before his call, President Nelson invited us to more deeply study the 2,200 references of the name Jesus Christ listed in the Topical Guide.
footnote_text: See Russell M. Nelson, “Prophets, Leadership, and Divine Law” (worldwide devotional for young adults, Jan. 8, 2017), broadcasts.ChurchofJesusChrist.org.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: “… Our focus [becomes] riveted on the Savior and His gospel.”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “Drawing the Power of Jesus Christ into Our Lives,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2017, 40–41.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: The Savior said, “Look unto me in every thought.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: In emphasizing the name of the Church, President Nelson taught, “If we … are to have access to the power of the Atonement of Jesus Christ—to cleanse and heal us, to strengthen and magnify us, and ultimately to exalt us—we must clearly acknowledge Him as the source of that power.”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “The Correct Name of the Church,” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2018, 88.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: Are there images of the Savior in our homes? Do we talk often to our children about the parables of Jesus? “The stories of Jesus [are] like a rushing wind across the embers of faith in the hearts of our children.”
footnote_text: Neil L. Andersen, “Tell Me the Stories of Jesus,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2010, 108.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: “We talk of Christ, we rejoice in Christ, … that our children may know to what source they may look for a remission of their sins.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: This same scripture adds that “we preach of Christ.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: Thirty years ago, President Dallin H. Oaks spoke of a letter he had received “from a man who said he had attended [a sacrament] meeting and listened to seventeen testimonies without hearing the Savior mentioned.”
footnote_text: Dallin H. Oaks, “Another Testament of Jesus Christ” (Brigham Young University fireside, June 6, 1993), 7, speeches.byu.edu.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: President Oaks then noted, “Perhaps that description is exaggerated [but] I quote it because it provides a vivid reminder for all of us.”
footnote_text: Dallin H. Oaks, “Witnesses of Christ,” Ensign, Nov. 1990, 30.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: With those around us, let us be more open, more willing to talk of Christ. President Nelson said, “True disciples of Jesus Christ are willing to stand out, speak up, and be different from the people of the world.”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “Drawing the Power of Jesus Christ into Our Lives,” 40.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: Sometimes we think that a conversation with someone needs to result in them coming to church or seeing the missionaries. Let the Lord guide them as they are willing, while we think more about our responsibility to be a voice for Him, thoughtful and open about our faith. Elder Dieter F. Uchtdorf has taught us that when someone asks us about our weekend, we should be willing to happily respond that we loved hearing the Primary children sing, “I’m trying to be like Jesus.”
footnote_text: See Dieter F. Uchtdorf, “Missionary Work: Sharing What Is in Your Heart,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2019, 17; “I’m Trying to Be like Jesus,” Children’s Songbook, 78.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: Be more open on social media in talking about your trust in Christ. Most will respect your faith, but if someone is dismissive when you speak of the Savior, take courage in His promise: “Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you … for my sake. … For great is your reward in heaven.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: We care more about being His followers than being “liked” by our own followers. Peter counseled, “Be ready always to give an answer [for] the hope that is in you.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: The Book of Mormon is a powerful witness of Jesus Christ. Virtually every page testifies of the Savior and His divine mission.
footnote_text: “As [the Book of Mormon prophetic scribes] wrote their testimonies of the promised Messiah, they mentioned some form of his name on an average of every 1.7 verses. [They] referred to Jesus Christ by, literally, 101 different names. … When we realize that a verse usually consists of one sentence, it appears that we cannot, on the average, read two sentences in the Book of Mormon without seeing some form of Christ’s name” (Susan Easton Black, Finding Christ through the Book of Mormon [1987], 5, 15). “While the words atone or atonement, in any of their forms, appear only once in the King James translation of the New Testament, they appear 35 times in the Book of Mormon. As another testament of Jesus Christ, it sheds precious light on His Atonement” (Russell M. Nelson, “The Atonement,” Ensign, Nov. 1996, 35).

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: Some of our fellow Christians are, at times, uncertain about our beliefs and motives. Let us genuinely rejoice with them in our shared faith in Jesus Christ and in the New Testament scriptures we all love. In the days ahead, those who believe in Jesus Christ will need the friendship and support of one another.
footnote_text: Those leaving Christianity in the United States are younger. “More than eight-in-ten members of the Silent Generation (those born between 1928 and 1945) describe themselves as Christians (84%), as do three-quarters of Baby Boomers (76%). In stark contrast, only half of Millennials (49%) describe themselves as Christians; four-in-ten are religious ‘nones,’ and one-in-ten Millennials identify with non-Christian faiths” (“In U.S., Decline of Christianity Continues,” pewforum.org).

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: As the world speaks less of Jesus Christ, let us speak more of Him. As our true colors as His disciples are revealed, many around us will be prepared to listen. As we share the light we have received from Him, His light and His transcendent saving power will shine on those willing to open their hearts. Jesus said, “I … come [as] a light into the world.”

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: Nothing lifts my desire to speak of Christ more than visualizing His return. While we do not know when He will come, the events of His return will be breathtaking! He will come in the clouds of heaven in majesty and glory with all His holy angels. Not just a few angels but all His holy angels. These are not the cherry-cheeked cherubim painted by Raphael, found on our Valentine cards. These are the angels of the centuries, the angels sent to shut the mouths of lions,

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: to open prison doors,

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: to announce His long-awaited birth,

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: to comfort Him in Gethsemane,

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: to assure His disciples at His Ascension,

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ

footnote_text: See Doctrine and Covenants 13; 27:12–13; 110:11–16; Joseph Smith—History 1:27–54.

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: Can you imagine being caught up to meet Him, whether on this side or the other side of the veil?

speaker: Neil L. Andersen
title: We Talk of Christ
context: My dear friends across the world, let us talk of Christ, anticipating His glorious promise: “Whosoever … shall confess me before men, him will I confess … before my Father.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: For the more than 36 years I’ve been an Apostle, the doctrine of the gathering of Israel has captured my attention.
footnote_text: I have spoken of Israel in at least 378 of the more than 800 messages I have delivered during my 36 years as an Apostle.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: Everything about it has intrigued me, including the ministries and names
footnote_text: In Hebrew, Abram is a noble name meaning “exalted father.” But when God changed that name to Abraham, the name took on even greater significance, meaning “father of a multitude.” Indeed, Abraham was to be the “father of many nations.” (See Genesis 17:5; Nehemiah 9:7.)

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; their lives and their wives; the covenant God made with them and extended through their lineage;
footnote_text: The Lord God Jehovah made a covenant with Abraham that the Savior of the world would be born through Abraham’s seed, certain lands would be inherited, and all nations would be blessed through Abraham’s lineage (see Bible Dictionary, “Abraham, covenant of”).

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: So imagine my delight when I was led recently to a new insight. With the help of two Hebrew scholars, I learned that one of the Hebraic meanings of the word Israel is “let God prevail.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: The word willing is crucial to this interpretation of Israel.
footnote_text: The word Israel appears more than a thousand times in the scriptures. It can apply to Jacob’s (Israel’s) family of 12 sons, plus daughters (see Genesis 35:23–26; 46:7). Today it can apply geographically as a place on planet Earth. But its doctrinal use applies to people who are willing to let God prevail in their lives.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: For a moment, let us recall a crucial turning point in the life of Jacob, the grandson of Abraham. At the place Jacob named Peniel (which means “the face of God”),
footnote_text: See Genesis 32:30; also spelled as Penuel in Genesis 32:31.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: Jacob wrestled with a serious challenge. His agency was tested. Through this wrestle, Jacob proved what was most important to him. He demonstrated that he was willing to let God prevail in his life. In response, God changed Jacob’s name to Israel,

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: meaning “let God prevail.” God then promised Israel that all the blessings that had been pronounced upon Abraham’s head would also be his.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: Sadly, Israel’s posterity broke their covenants with God. They stoned the prophets and were not willing to let God prevail in their lives. Subsequently, God scattered them to the four corners of the earth.
footnote_text: For further study, see Topical Guide, “Israel, Scattering of.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: Mercifully, He later promised to gather them, as reported by Isaiah: “For a small moment have I forsaken thee [Israel]; but with great mercies will I gather thee.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: For centuries, prophets have foretold this gathering,

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: This premillennial gathering is an individual saga of expanding faith and spiritual courage for millions of people. And as members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, or “latter-day covenant Israel,”
footnote_text: See Encyclopedia of Mormonism (1992), “Covenant Israel, Latter-Day,” 1:330–31.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: we have been charged to assist the Lord with this pivotal work.
footnote_text: As we participate in the gathering of Israel, the Lord has a wonderful way of describing those being gathered. He refers to us collectively as His “peculiar treasure” (Exodus 19:5; Psalm 135:4), as His “jewels” (Malachi 3:17; Doctrine and Covenants 101:3), and as a “holy nation” (Exodus 19:6; see also Deuteronomy 14:2; 26:18).

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: We may be led to some who have never believed in God or Jesus Christ but who are now yearning to learn about Them and Their plan of happiness. Others may have been “born in the covenant”
footnote_text: This phrase refers to the very covenant that God made with Abraham, saying, “In thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed” (3 Nephi 20:27). “Born in the covenant” means that before a person was born, that person’s mother and father were sealed in the temple.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: The gospel net to gather scattered Israel is expansive. There is room for each person who will fully embrace the gospel of Jesus Christ. Each convert becomes one of God’s covenant children,
footnote_text: Such a promise was taught by God to Abraham: “As many as receive this Gospel shall be called after thy name, and shall be accounted thy seed, and shall rise up and bless thee, as their father” (Abraham 2:10; see also Romans 8:14–17; Galatians 3:26–29).

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: whether by birth or by adoption. Each becomes a full heir to all that God has promised the faithful children of Israel!
footnote_text: Each faithful member may request a patriarchal blessing. Through the inspiration of the Holy Ghost, the patriarch declares that person’s lineage in the house of Israel. That declaration is not necessarily a pronouncement of his or her race, nationality, or genetic makeup. Rather, the declared lineage identifies the tribe of Israel through which that individual will receive his or her blessings.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: Each of us has a divine potential because each is a child of God. Each is equal in His eyes. The implications of this truth are profound. Brothers and sisters, please listen carefully to what I am about to say. God does not love one race more than another. His doctrine on this matter is clear. He invites all to come unto Him, “black and white, bond and free, male and female.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: The question for each of us, regardless of race, is the same. Are you willing to let God prevail in your life? Are you willing to let God be the most important influence in your life? Will you allow His words, His commandments, and His covenants to influence what you do each day? Will you allow His voice to take priority over any other? Are you willing to let whatever He needs you to do take precedence over every other ambition? Are you willing to have your will swallowed up in His?
footnote_text: See Mosiah 15:7. Being of Israel is not for the faint of heart. To receive all the blessings that God has in store for Abraham’s seed, we can each expect to be given our own unique “Abrahamic test.” God will test us, as the Prophet Joseph Smith taught, by wrenching our very heartstrings. (See recollection of John Taylor in Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Joseph Smith [2007], 231.)

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: Now, my dear brothers and sisters, it takes both faith and courage to let God prevail. It takes persistent, rigorous spiritual work to repent and to put off the natural man through the Atonement of Jesus Christ.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: During these perilous times of which the Apostle Paul prophesied,

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: Now, how does the Lord feel about people who will let God prevail? Nephi summed it up well: “[The Lord] loveth those who will have him to be their God. Behold, he loved our fathers, and he covenanted with them, yea, even Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and he remember[s] the covenants which he [has] made.”

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: And what is the Lord willing to do for Israel? The Lord has pledged that He will “fight [our] battles, and [our] children’s battles, and our children’s children’s [battles] … to the third and fourth generation”!
footnote_text: Doctrine and Covenants 98:37; see also Psalm 31:23; Isaiah 49:25; Doctrine and Covenants 105:14.

speaker: Russell M. Nelson
title: Let God Prevail
context: My dear brothers and sisters, as you choose to let God prevail in your lives, you will experience for yourselves that our God is “a God of miracles.”

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Tested, Proved, and Polished
context: “And they who keep their first estate shall be added upon; and they who keep not their first estate shall not have glory in the same kingdom with those who keep their first estate; and they who keep their second estate shall have glory added upon their heads for ever and ever.”

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Tested, Proved, and Polished
context: Heavenly Father and Jesus Christ know and love you. They want you to return to Them and become like Them. Your success is Their success. You have felt that love confirmed by the Holy Ghost when you have read or heard these words: “For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.”

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Tested, Proved, and Polished
context: God has the power to make our way easier. He fed manna to the children of Israel in their wandering to the promised land. The Lord in His mortal ministry healed the sick, raised the dead, and calmed the sea. After His Resurrection, He opened “the prison to them that were bound.”

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Tested, Proved, and Polished
context: Yet the Prophet Joseph Smith, one of the greatest of His prophets, suffered in prison and was taught the lesson we all profit from and need in our recurring tests of faith: “And if thou shouldst be cast into the pit, or into the hands of murderers, and the sentence of death passed upon thee; if thou be cast into the deep; if the billowing surge conspire against thee; if fierce winds become thine enemy; if the heavens gather blackness, and all the elements combine to hedge up the way; and above all, if the very jaws of hell shall gape open the mouth wide after thee, know thou, my son, that all these things shall give thee experience, and shall be for thy good.”

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Tested, Proved, and Polished
context: “And he will take upon him death, that he may loose the bands of death which bind his people; and he will take upon him their infirmities, that his bowels may be filled with mercy, according to the flesh, that he may know according to the flesh how to succor his people according to their infirmities.”

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Tested, Proved, and Polished
context: “Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.”

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Tested, Proved, and Polished
context: “For after much tribulation come the blessings.”

title: Tested, Proved, and Polished
context: In this, the Lord is our Exemplar. On the cross of Golgotha, having already suffered pain so great that He would have died were He not the Begotten Son of God, He looked on His executioners and said to His Father, “Forgive them; for they know not what they do.”

speaker: Henry B. Eyring
title: Tested, Proved, and Polished
context: “Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.”

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: Earlier this year, as the pandemic accelerated, the First Presidency pledged that “the Church and its members will faithfully exhibit our commitment to being good citizens and good neighbors”

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: and will “use an abundance of caution.”

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: The prophet Nephi began engraving the small plates when he was a grown man. As he looked back on his life and ministry, he offered an important reflection in the very first verse of the Book of Mormon. This verse frames an important principle for us to consider in our time. Following his familiar words, “I, Nephi, having been born of goodly parents … ,” he writes, “and having seen many afflictions in the course of my days, nevertheless, having been highly favored of the Lord in all my days.”

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: We read of Paul and Silas, who, while imprisoned in stocks, prayed, sang, taught, testified—and even baptized the jailer.

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: And again of Paul, in Rome, who was under house arrest for two years, during which time he continually “expounded and testified the kingdom of God,”

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: “teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ.”

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: Of Nephi and Lehi, the sons of Helaman, who after abuse and imprisonment were encircled by a fire of protection as the Lord’s “still voice of perfect mildness … did pierce [their captors] even to the very soul.”

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: Of Alma and Amulek in Ammonihah, who found that many “did believe … and began to repent, and to search the scriptures,”

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: even though they were then mocked and without food, water, or clothes, bound and confined in prison.

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord

context: and “God shall be with you forever.”

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord

We need an adjustment to this pattern. … A home-centered Church, supported by what takes place inside our … buildings.”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “Opening Remarks,” Ensign or Liahona, Nov. 2018, 7.

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: In 2018, President Nelson introduced ministering as an adjustment “in the way we care for each other.”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “Let Us All Press On,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2018, 118.

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: “… Shall we not go on in so great a cause? Go forward and not backward. Courage, … and on, on to the victory! Let your hearts rejoice, and be exceedingly glad. Let the earth break forth into singing.”

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: Brothers and sisters, I believe that one day, each of you will look back at the canceled events, the sadness, the disappointments, and the loneliness attendant to the challenging times we are passing through to see them overshadowed by choice blessings and increased faith and testimonies. I believe that in this life, and in the life to come, your afflictions, your Ammonihah, your Liberty Jail, will be consecrated for your gain.

speaker: Gary E. Stevenson
title: Highly Favored of the Lord
context: I close with my testimony of Jesus Christ, who Himself was no stranger to affliction and as part of His infinite Atonement descended below all things.

speaker: Milton Camargo
title: Ask, Seek, and Knock
context: Four months ago, in my study of the scriptures, I was reading about Alma’s mission in Ammonihah when I came across this suggestion in Come, Follow Me: “As you read about the great blessings God gave the people of Nephi (see Alma 9:19–23), ponder the great blessings He has given you.”
footnote_text: Come, Follow Me—For Individuals and Families: Book of Mormon 2020 (2019), 91.

speaker: Milton Camargo
title: Ask, Seek, and Knock
context: Our prophet, President Russell M. Nelson, has given a similar invitation in our day. He said: “Pray in the name of Jesus Christ about your concerns, your fears, your weaknesses—yes, the very longings of your heart. And then listen! Write the thoughts that come to your mind. Record your feelings and follow through with actions that you are prompted to take. As you repeat this process day after day, month after month, year after year, you will ‘grow into the principle of revelation.’”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2018, 95; quoting Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Joseph Smith (2007), 132.

speaker: Milton Camargo
title: Ask, Seek, and Knock
context: President Nelson added, “In coming days, it will not be possible to survive spiritually without the guiding, directing, comforting, and constant influence of the Holy Ghost.”
footnote_text: Russell M. Nelson, “Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives,” 96.

speaker: Milton Camargo
title: Ask, Seek, and Knock
context: Recently a loved one said to me, “I believe personal revelation to be true. I believe the Holy Ghost will show me all things I should do.

speaker: Milton Camargo
title: Ask, Seek, and Knock
context: It is easy to believe when I feel my bosom burn with undoubting conviction.

speaker: Milton Camargo
title: Ask, Seek, and Knock

footnote_text: “Microwaves use microwave sound energy waves to heat up food or liquids. There has to be something inside the microwave to absorb these waves. Running a microwave with nothing in it will damage the magnetron and other parts of the microwave as well. In a worst case scenario, the microwave parts will overheat and possibly catch fire” (Abacus Appliance Service Corporation, “Will I Destroy My Microwave If It Runs Empty?” Aug. 16, 2012, abacusappliance.com; see also Julie R. title: Essential Conversations
context: Have you ever wondered why we call Primary “Primary”? While the name refers to spiritual learning children receive in their earliest years, to me it is also a reminder of a powerful truth. To our Heavenly Father, children have never been secondary—they have always been “primary.”

speaker: Joy D. Jones
title: Essential Conversations
context: He trusts us to value, respect, and protect them as children of God. That means we never harm them physically, verbally, or emotionally in any way, even when tensions and pressures run high. Instead we value children, and we do all we can to combat the evils of abuse. Their care is primary to us—as it is to Him.
footnote_text: See Michaelene P. Grassli, “Behold Your Little Ones,” Ensign, Nov. 1992, 93: “To me, the word behold is significant. It implies more than just ‘look and see.’ When the Lord instructed the Nephites to behold their little ones, I believe he told them to give attention to their children, to contemplate them, to look beyond the present and see their eternal possibilities.” See also Russell M. Nelson, “Listen to Learn,” Ensign, May 1991, 22: “To rule children by force is the technique of Satan, not of the Savior. No, we don’t own our children. Our parental privilege is to love them, to lead them, and to let them go.”

speaker: Joy D. Jones
title: Essential Conversations
